title.zh: 卷三百三十九 列傳第九十八 蘇轍族孫:元老
title.en: Volume 339 Biographies 98: Su Zhezu and grandson: Yuanlao
title.raw: 卷三百三十九 列傳第九十八 蘇轍族孫:元老 Volume 339 Biographies 98: Su Zhezu and grandson: Yuanlao

sentences.zh: 蘇轍，字子由，年十九，與兄軾同登進士科，又同策制舉。

translations.literal: Su Zhe, style name Ziyou, at nineteen years of age passed the jinshi examination together with his elder brother Shi, and together also sat the policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe, courtesy name Ziyou, was nineteen when he and his elder brother Shi both passed the jinshi examination and were examined together in the policy test as well.

sentences.zh: 仁宗春秋高，轍慮或倦於勤，因極言得失，而於禁廷之事，尤為切至。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was advanced in years; Zhe feared he might grow weary of diligence, and therefore spoke to the utmost of gains and losses, while on affairs within the forbidden court he was especially penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong was growing old, and Zhe worried that the emperor might slacken in his diligence. He therefore spoke at length about what had gone right and wrong, and was especially blunt about matters within the inner court.

sentences.zh: 曰：

translations.literal: He said:
translations.idiomatic: He said:

sentences.zh: 「陛下即位三十餘年矣，平居靜慮，亦嘗有憂於此乎，無憂於此乎？

translations.literal: "Your Majesty has been on the throne for more than thirty years; in quiet moments of reflection, have you sometimes been troubled by this, or not troubled by it?
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty has reigned for more than thirty years. In your quiet moments, have you ever brooded over this—or have you never brooded at all?

sentences.zh: 臣伏讀制策，陛下既有憂懼之言矣。

translations.literal: Your subject has read the policy examination topics, and Your Majesty already has words of worry and fear in them.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the examination topics, your subject sees that Your Majesty has already expressed concern and apprehension there.

sentences.zh: 然臣愚不敏，竊意陛下有其言耳，未有其實也。

translations.literal: Yet your subject, foolish and unperceptive, ventures to think that Your Majesty has these words but not yet this reality.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my dull inadequacy I venture to suspect that Your Majesty has the words, but not yet the deed.

sentences.zh: 往者寶元、慶曆之間，西夏作難，陛下晝不安坐，夜不安席，天下皆謂陛下憂懼小心如周文王。

translations.literal: In the past, between the Baoyuan and Qingli periods, the Western Xia made trouble; Your Majesty could not sit at ease by day nor lie at ease by night; all under Heaven said Your Majesty's worried caution was like King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Xi Xia rose in revolt during the Baoyuan and Qingli years, Your Majesty could not sit easy by day or rest easy by night; the empire took you for a ruler as anxiously careful as King Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 然自西方解兵，陛下棄置憂懼之心，二十年矣。

translations.literal: Yet since the western troubles were settled, Your Majesty has cast aside a heart of worry and fear for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: But since peace returned to the west, Your Majesty has set aside such vigilant anxiety for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 古之聖人，無事則深憂，有事則不懼。

translations.literal: The sages of antiquity, when there were no affairs, were deeply worried; when there were affairs, they were not afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sages worried deeply in times of peace and did not panic when trouble came.

sentences.zh: 夫無事而深憂者，所以為有事之不懼也。

translations.literal: That one is deeply worried when there are no affairs is how one makes oneself not afraid when there are affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deep worry in time of peace is precisely what makes fearlessness possible when crisis arrives.

sentences.zh: 今陛下無事則不憂，有事則大懼，臣以為憂樂之節易矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, when there are no affairs, is not worried; when there are affairs, is greatly afraid; your subject thinks the order of worry and ease has been reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty is unworried when all is calm yet terrified when trouble comes—I believe worry and complacency have been reversed.

sentences.zh: 臣疏遠小臣，聞之道路，不知信否？

translations.literal: Your subject, a distant and minor official, heard it on the road and does not know whether it is true or not?
translations.idiomatic: I am only a remote junior official who has heard this in the streets and cannot say whether it is true.

sentences.zh: 近歲以來，宮中貴姬至以千數，歌舞飲酒，優笑無度，坐朝不聞咨謨，便殿無所顧問。

translations.literal: In recent years, the favored ladies within the palace have reached a total of thousands; song, dance, drink, and wine, jest and laughter without limit; sitting at court one does not hear consultation and deliberation, in the side hall there is no asking or inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the palace's favored consorts have numbered in the thousands; there is endless singing, feasting, and laughter; at court Your Majesty does not hear counsel debated, and in the privy chambers no one is questioned.

sentences.zh: 三代之衰，漢、唐之季，女寵之害，陛下亦知之矣。

translations.literal: The decay of the Three Dynasties, the late years of Han and Tang—the harm of female favor Your Majesty also knows.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows as well how female favor ruined the Three Dynasties and brought down the late Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 久而不止，百蠹將由之而出。

translations.literal: If this long continues without stopping, a hundred harms will issue from it.
translations.idiomatic: If this continues unchecked, a hundred evils will spring from it.

sentences.zh: 內則蠱惑之所汙，以傷和伐性；

translations.literal: Within, what seduction pollutes will wound harmony and consume the vital nature;
translations.idiomatic: Within, seduction will corrupt the person, harm harmony, and wear away the body;

sentences.zh: 外則私謁之所亂，以敗政害事。

translations.literal: without, what private audiences disorder will defeat government and harm affairs.
translations.idiomatic: without, private access will disorder administration and ruin public business.

sentences.zh: 陛下無謂好色于內，不害外事也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should not think that being fond of beauty within does not harm external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not suppose that fondness for beauty within the palace does no harm to affairs outside it.

sentences.zh: 今海內窮困，生民愁苦，而宮中好賜不為限極，所欲則給，不問有無。

translations.literal: Now within the seas there is hardship and distress, the people live in bitterness, yet within the palace generous bestowals know no limit—what is desired is given, without asking whether there is or is not.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is exhausted and the people groan under hardship, yet within the palace lavish grants know no limit—whatever is desired is supplied, with no question whether funds exist.

sentences.zh: 司會不敢爭，大臣不敢諫，執契持敕，迅若兵火。

translations.literal: The Director of Accounts dares not contend, great ministers dare not remonstrate; holding the tally and presenting the edict, swift as fire and sword.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Accounts dares not object, the chief ministers dare not remonstrate—they bear tally and edict and move swift as blade and flame.

sentences.zh: 國家內有養士、養兵之費，外有契丹、西夏之奉，陛下又自為一阱以耗其遺餘，臣恐陛下以此得謗，而民心不歸也。」

translations.literal: Within the state there are expenses for nurturing scholars and soldiers, without there are the tributes to Khitan and Western Xia; Your Majesty moreover sets a trap of your own to consume what remains; your subject fears Your Majesty will on this account earn blame, and the people's hearts will not turn to you."
translations.idiomatic: Within we spend on scholars and soldiers, without we pay Khitan and Xi Xia—and Your Majesty has added a pit of your own to swallow what is left. I fear Your Majesty will earn reproach on this account and the people's hearts will turn away."

sentences.zh: 策入，轍自謂必見黜。

translations.literal: When the answer was submitted, Zhe himself expected certainly to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When his examination answer went in, Zhe fully expected to be cashiered.

sentences.zh: 考官司馬光第以三等，范鎮難之。

translations.literal: Examining official Sima Guang ranked it third class; Fan Zhen found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Examiner Sima Guang placed it in the third rank, but Fan Zhen objected.

sentences.zh: 蔡襄曰：「吾三司使也，司會之言，吾愧之而不敢怨。」

translations.literal: Cai Xiang said: "I am Director of the Three Bureaus; as to the Director of Accounts' words, I am ashamed of them but dare not resent them."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang said, "I am Director of the Three Commissariat Bureaus. What the Director of Accounts said shames me, yet I dare not resent it."

sentences.zh: 惟考官胡宿以為不遜，請黜之。

translations.literal: Only examiner Hu Su thought it insubordinate and asked that he be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Only examiner Hu Su deemed it insubordinate and asked that Zhe be rejected.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「以直言召人，而以直言棄之，天下其謂我何？」

translations.literal: Renzong said: "To summon a man for outspoken words and then to discard him for outspoken words—what will All under Heaven say of me?"
translations.idiomatic: Renzong said, "If I summon men for frank speech and then discard them for frank speech, what will the world say of me?"

sentences.zh: 宰相不得已，置之下等，授商州軍事推官。

translations.literal: The chief ministers had no choice; they placed him in the lowest grade and appointed him Military Push Officer of Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers yielded and ranked him in the lowest grade, appointing him military push officer in Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時父洵被命修《禮書》，兄軾簽書鳳翔判官。

translations.literal: At that time his father Xun had been ordered to compile the Book of Rites, and his elder brother Shi was signing secretary as assistant magistrate of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun was then ordered to compile the Book of Rites, and his brother Shi was signing secretary on the Fengxiang prefectural bench.

sentences.zh: 轍乞養親京師。

translations.literal: Zhe begged to support his parents in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe petitioned to remain in the capital to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 三年，軾還，轍為大名推官。

translations.literal: In the third year Shi returned; Zhe became push officer of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shi returned, and Zhe took a push-officer post at Daming.

sentences.zh: 逾年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: After a year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he buried his father and entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，神宗立已二年，轍上書言事，召對延和殿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Shenzong had already been on the throne two years; Zhe submitted a memorial on affairs and was summoned for audience in the Yanhe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Shenzong had been enthroned two years. Zhe submitted a memorial and was called to audience in the Yanhe Hall.

sentences.zh: 時王安石以執政與陳升之領三司條例，命轍為之屬。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Anshi, holding office as chancellor together with Chen Shengzhi, oversaw the Three Bureaus Regulations; [the emperor] ordered Zhe to serve under them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was then chancellor, jointly overseeing the Three Bureaus reforms with Chen Shengzhi, and Zhe was appointed to his staff.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿附安石，轍與論多相牾。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing attached himself to Anshi; Zhe in debate with him often clashed.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing sided with Anshi; Zhe often crossed him in argument.

sentences.zh: 安石出《青苗書》使轍熟議，曰：「有不便，以告勿疑。」

translations.literal: Anshi produced the Green Sprouts book for Zhe to study thoroughly, saying: "If there is inconvenience, report it—do not doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi handed him the Green Sprouts treatise and told him to study it closely: "Tell me of any inconvenience you find—do not hesitate."

sentences.zh: 轍曰：「以錢貸民，使出息二分，本以救民，非為利也。

translations.literal: Zhe said: "To lend money to the people and have them pay interest of two parts in ten—the original intent was to rescue the people, not to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe replied, "Lending money to the people at twenty percent interest was meant to relieve distress, not to turn a profit.

sentences.zh: 然出納之際，吏緣為奸，雖有法不能禁，錢入民手，雖良民不免妄用；

translations.literal: Yet in the intervals of disbursement and receipt, clerks take occasion to commit fraud; though there be law they cannot be forbidden; when money enters the people's hands, even good commoners cannot avoid misuse;
translations.idiomatic: Yet at every hand-out and collection clerks will twist it into corruption; laws cannot stop them; once cash is in common hands even honest folk spend it rashly;

sentences.zh: 及其納錢，雖富民不免逾限。

translations.literal: and when they repay the money, even wealthy commoners cannot avoid exceeding limits.
translations.idiomatic: and when repayment comes due even well-to-do households fall behind.

sentences.zh: 如此，則恐鞭箠必用，州縣之事不勝煩矣。

translations.literal: If so, then I fear the lash will surely be used and the business of prefectures and counties will be more than they can bear in annoyance.
translations.idiomatic: Then the rod will surely be used and prefectures and counties will be buried in trouble.

sentences.zh: 唐劉晏掌國計，未嘗有所假貸。

translations.literal: In Tang, Liu Yan managed state accounts and never lent on loan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, Liu Yan ran the national accounts and never made loans.

sentences.zh: 有尤之者，晏曰：『使民僥倖得錢，非國之福；

translations.literal: There were those who especially blamed him; Yan said: 'To let the people obtain money by luck is not the state's blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Some censured him, but Yan said, "Letting the people seize lucky windfalls is no blessing to the state;

sentences.zh: 使吏倚法督責，非民之便。

translations.literal: to make clerks rely on law to supervise and collect is no convenience to the people.
translations.idiomatic: and making clerks lean on the law to dun and collect is no benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 吾雖未嘗假貸，而四方豐凶貴賤，知之未嘗逾時。

translations.literal: Though I have never lent on loan, yet in the four quarters, abundance and famine, dearth and cheapness—I have never known it later than its time.
translations.idiomatic: Though I never lent, I never learned of scarcity or plenty, famine or glut in any quarter later than I should.

sentences.zh: 有賤必糴，有貴必糶，以此四方無甚貴、甚賤之病，安用貸為？』

translations.literal: Where there was cheapness he surely bought up; where there was dearness he surely sold down—by this the four quarters had no disease of extreme dearth or extreme cheapness; why employ lending?'
translations.idiomatic: When grain was cheap he bought; when it was dear he sold—so the realm suffered neither extreme famine nor extreme glut. Why borrow to the people at all?

sentences.zh: 晏之所言，則常平法耳。

translations.literal: What Yan spoke of was then the Ever-Normal Granary method.
translations.idiomatic: What Yan described was simply the Ever-Normal method.

sentences.zh: 今此法見在而患不修，公誠能有意於民，舉而行之，則晏之功可立俟也。」

translations.literal: Now this method exists in present practice yet the worry is it is not repaired; if your lordship can truly intend benefit for the people and lift it and practice it, then Yan's achievement can be awaited standing."
translations.idiomatic: That method is still on the books but neglected. If you truly mean to aid the people and revive it, Yan's achievement can be matched at once."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「君言誠有理，當徐思之。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Your words truly have reason; I shall ponder them slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "There is force in what you say. I shall think on it."

sentences.zh: 自此逾月不言青苗。

translations.literal: From this for more than a month he did not speak of Green Sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: For a month thereafter he did not mention Green Sprouts again.

sentences.zh: 會河北轉運判官王廣廉奏乞度僧牒數千為本錢，于陝西漕司私行青苗法，春散秋斂，與安石意合，於是青苗法遂行。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Guanglian, transport commissioner of Hebei, memorialized begging to count several thousand monk certificates as capital, and at the Shaanxi Commissariat bureau privately to practice the Green Sprouts law—disbursing in spring and collecting in autumn—which matched Anshi's intent; thereupon the Green Sprouts law was then put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Then Hebei transport judge Wang Guanglian asked to sell thousands of ordination certificates for capital and to run a private Green Sprouts scheme through the Shaanxi commissariat—spring disbursement, autumn collection—in line with Anshi's intent, and the law took effect.

sentences.zh: 安石因遣八使之四方，訪求遺利。

translations.literal: Anshi thereupon dispatched eight envoys to the four quarters to seek profits left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi then sent eight commissioners to the provinces to ferret out unexploited revenue.

sentences.zh: 中外知其必迎合生事，皆莫敢言。

translations.literal: Within and without, all knew they would surely toady and stir up affairs; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country knew they would only manufacture trouble to please him; no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 轍往見陳升之曰：「昔嘉祐末，遣使寬恤諸路，各務生事，還奏多不可行，為天下笑。

translations.literal: Zhe went to see Chen Shengzhi and said: "In the late Jiayou years envoys were dispatched to show lenient relief in the circuits; each strove to stir up affairs; on return their memorials mostly could not be carried out and became the world's laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe went to Chen Shengzhi and said, "Late in Jiayou we sent agents to relieve the circuits; each invented work; their reports mostly could not be adopted and the empire laughed.

sentences.zh: 今何以異此？」

translations.literal: How is the present different from this?"
translations.idiomatic: How is today different?"

sentences.zh: 又以書抵安石，力陳其不可。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter reaching Anshi, strongly setting forth that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Anshi at length why the scheme would not work.

sentences.zh: 安石怒，將加以罪，升之止之，以為河南推官。

translations.literal: Anshi was angry and was about to punish him with a crime; Shengzhi stopped it and had him made push officer of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi wanted to punish him, but Shengzhi checked him and had Zhe made push officer of Henan.

sentences.zh: 會張方平知陳州，辟為教授。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Fangping governed Chen Prefecture and recruited him as professor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fangping was then prefect of Chenzhou and engaged him as professor.

sentences.zh: 三年，授齊州掌書記。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Recorder of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was appointed recorder at Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 又三年，改著作佐郎。

translations.literal: After another three years he was changed to Assistant Gentlemen for Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after that he was promoted to Assistant Gentlemen for Drafting.

sentences.zh: 復從方平簽書南京判官。

translations.literal: Again he followed Fangping as signing secretary on the Nanjing prefectural bench.
translations.idiomatic: He again served Fangping as signing secretary on the Nanjing bench.

sentences.zh: 居二年，坐兄軾以詩得罪，謫監筠州鹽酒稅，五年不得調。

translations.literal: After two years, because his elder brother Shi offended in a poem he was demoted to supervisor of the Jizhou salt and wine tax; for five years he received no transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, when his brother Shi offended in verse, he was demoted to supervisor of the Jizhou salt and wine tax and went five years without reassignment.

sentences.zh: 移知績溪縣。

translations.literal: He was moved to govern Jixi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to serve as magistrate of Jixi County.

sentences.zh: 司馬光以王安石雇役之害，欲復差役，不知其害相半於雇役。

translations.literal: Sima Guang, because of the harms of Wang Anshi's hired-service [tax], wished to restore the corvée service system but did not know its harms were half those of hired service.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang, seeing the harm of Wang Anshi's hired-labor tax, wished to restore corvée labor but did not see that corvée brought harms half as grave again.

sentences.zh: 轍言：「自罷差役僅二十年，吏民皆未習慣。

translations.literal: Zhe said: "Since the corvée was abolished it has been barely twenty years; clerks and people are all not yet accustomed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "Corvée has been abolished only twenty years; officials and commoners alike are still unaccustomed to the change.

sentences.zh: 況役法關涉眾事，根芽盤錯，行之徐緩，乃得審詳。

translations.literal: Moreover the service law touches many affairs and its roots and shoots are tangled and interlocked; to practice it slowly and gradually is how one can get it examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The service law touches countless matters and its roots are hopelessly tangled; only a slow and careful restoration can be thoroughly weighed.

sentences.zh: 若不窮究首尾，忽遽便行，恐既行之後，別生諸弊。

translations.literal: If one does not exhaust beginning and end but hastily and suddenly practices it, I fear after it has been practiced other harms will separately arise.
translations.idiomatic: If we rush it without tracing every consequence, new abuses will surely appear once it is in force.

sentences.zh: 今州縣役錢，例有積年寬剩，大約足支數年，且依舊雇役，盡今年而止。

translations.literal: Now the service money of prefectures and counties by rule has accumulated surplus over many years; on the whole it suffices to support several years; for the time let hired service continue as of old and stop entirely this year.
translations.idiomatic: Today counties still hold years of surplus service funds, enough to last several years. Let hired service continue unchanged through this year only.

sentences.zh: 催督有司審議差役，趁今冬成法，來年役使鄉戶。

translations.literal: Urge the responsible offices to deliberate corvée in detail; seize this winter to complete the statute; next year let rural households perform service.
translations.idiomatic: Press the ministries to draft a corvée statute by winter and draft rural households next year.

sentences.zh: 但使既行之後，無復人言，則進退皆便。」

translations.literal: Only if after it has been practiced there is no further popular complaint, then advance and retreat are all convenient."
translations.idiomatic: If afterward there is no public outcry, whether we keep or change the policy will be straightforward."

sentences.zh: 光又以安石私設《詩》、《書新義》考試天下士，欲改科舉，別為新格。

translations.literal: Guang also because Anshi privately set new interpretations of the Classic of Poetry and Classic of Documents to examine the empire's scholars wished to change the civil service examinations and separately make a new format.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also wished to change the examinations because Anshi had imposed his private new interpretations of the Odes and Documents on candidates nationwide.

sentences.zh: 轍言：「進士來年秋試，日月無幾，而議不時決。

translations.literal: Zhe said: "Jinshi come the autumn of next year for examination; days and months are few, yet deliberation is not decided in time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "Jinshi candidates face the autumn examination next year with little time left, yet policy is still undecided.

sentences.zh: 詩賦雖小技，比次聲律，用功不淺。

translations.literal: Poetry and fu, though minor arts, in arranging tonal patterns require study not shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry and fu are minor arts, yet matching tone and meter takes serious effort.

sentences.zh: 至於治經，誦讀講解，尤不輕易。

translations.literal: As for studying the classics, reciting, reading, and explaining them is especially not light work.
translations.idiomatic: Classical study—memorizing, reading, and explaining—is still harder.

sentences.zh: 要之，來年皆未可施行。

translations.literal: In sum, none can be put into practice by next year.
translations.idiomatic: In short, nothing new can fairly take effect next year.

sentences.zh: 乞來年科場，一切如舊，惟經義兼取注疏及諸家論議，或出己見，不專用王氏學。

translations.literal: I beg that next year's examination field, everything be as of old; only in interpreting the classics take together commentaries and discussions of various schools, or produce one's own view, not exclusively using the Wang school.
translations.idiomatic: Let next year's field run entirely as before, but in classical exegesis accept commentaries and schools other than Wang Anshi's, or the candidate's own view.

sentences.zh: 仍罷律義，令舉人知有定論，一意為學，以待選試，然後徐議元祐五年以後科舉格式，未為晚也。」

translations.literal: Still abolish legal interpretation; let candidates know there is a fixed standard and single-mindedly study, waiting for selection examination; afterward gradually deliberate the examination format after the fifth year of Yuanyou—this would not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Drop the legal-interpretation test as well. Give candidates a settled standard to study toward; only after the examinations should we revise the Yuanyou format—that will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 光皆不能從。

translations.literal: Guang could follow none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Guang could not accept any of this.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗以夏國內亂，用兵攻討，乃於熙河增蘭州，于延安增安疆、米脂等五砦。

translations.literal: At the beginning Shenzong because the Xia state had internal disorder used troops to attack and punish; thereupon at Xihe he increased Lanzhou, and at Yan'an he increased Anjiang, Mizhi, and five other forts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xi Xia fell into civil strife Shenzong had campaigned in force, adding Lanzhou on the Xi River frontier and Anjiang, Mizhi, and five other forts around Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 二年，夏遣使賀登位，使還，未出境，又遣使入境。

translations.literal: In the second year Xia sent envoys to congratulate the accession; when the envoys returned, before leaving the border they again sent envoys to enter the territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Xi Xia sent envoys to congratulate his enthronement; before the first mission had left the border a second entered our territory.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其有請蘭州、五砦地意，大臣議棄守未決。

translations.literal: The court knew they intended to request Lanzhou and the five forts' territory; among great ministers deliberation to abandon and hold was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew they would ask for Lanzhou and the five forts; ministers had not yet agreed whether to hold or yield them.

sentences.zh: 轍言曰：「頃者西人雖至，疆場之事，初不自言。

translations.literal: Zhe said: "Not long since the western people though they had come to the border matters at first they did not speak themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "The Xi Xia envoys have come again, yet at the border they still will not raise their demand themselves.

sentences.zh: 度其狡心，蓋知朝廷厭兵，確然不請，欲使此議發自朝廷，得以為重。

translations.literal: Measuring their cunning heart, they probably know the court is weary of war and will certainly not request; they wish to make this deliberation issue from the court so they can make it weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Their craft is plain: knowing we are weary of war, they will not ask outright; they want the court to offer first so the grant weighs as a favor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷深覺其意，忍而不予，情得勢窮，始來請命，一失此機，必為後悔。

translations.literal: The court deeply perceived their intent and patiently did not give; when sentiment obtained and momentum was exhausted they first came to beg command; once this opportunity is lost one will surely regret afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The court sensed this and held back; when they were cornered they came to plead. Lose this moment and we will regret it.

sentences.zh: 彼若點集兵馬，屯聚境上，許之則畏兵而予，不復為恩；

translations.literal: If they rally troops and horses and mass at the border, if we grant then in fear of arms we grant and it is no longer grace;
translations.idiomatic: If they mass troops on the border and we yield under threat, the grant is no kindness;

sentences.zh: 不予則邊釁一開，禍難無已。

translations.literal: if we do not grant then the border quarrel opens once and disaster has no end.
translations.idiomatic: if we refuse, the frontier war opens and calamity will not end.

sentences.zh: 間不容髮，正在此時，不可失也。

translations.literal: No room for a hair to slip through—the time is exactly now; it cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: There is no margin for delay—the moment is now and must not be missed.

sentences.zh: 況今日之事，主上妙年，母后聽斷，將帥吏士，恩情未接，兵交之日，誰使效命？

translations.literal: Moreover today's affairs—the ruler is in splendid youth, the empress dowager hears and decides; generals, clerks, and scholar-officials—favor and feeling are not yet joined; on the day arms cross, who will be ordered to give their lives?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is young, the empress dowager regent, and generals and officials scarcely know one another. When battle comes, who will die for us?

sentences.zh: 若其羽書遝至，勝負紛然，臨機決斷，誰任其責？

translations.literal: If urgent reports arrive in succession and victory and defeat are tangled, who at the critical moment decides and who bears the responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: If urgent dispatches crowd in and fortune wavers, who will decide on the spot—and who will answer for it?

sentences.zh: 惟乞聖心以此反覆思慮，早賜裁斷，無使西人別致倡狂。」

translations.literal: Only beg the sage heart on this to reflect back and forth, early bestowing decision, not letting the western people separately cause violent madness."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this again and again and decide at once, lest Xi Xia grow reckless."

sentences.zh: 於是朝廷許還五砦，夏人遂服。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court permitted return of the five forts and the Xia people thereupon submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court yielded the five forts and Xi Xia submitted.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was moved to Gentleman Attendant-at-Audience and Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman Attendant-at-Audience and Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議回河故道，轍為公著言：「河決而北，自先帝不能回。

translations.literal: The court deliberated returning the Yellow River to its old course; Zhe spoke to Gong Zhu: "The river burst and went north; the former emperor himself could not return it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated forcing the Yellow River back to its old channel, Zhe told Gong Zhu, "Once the river burst northward even the late emperor could not turn it.

sentences.zh: 今不因其舊而修其未至，乃欲取而回之，其為力也難，而為責也重，是謂智勇勢力過先帝也。」

translations.literal: Now not following its old course to repair what has not yet reached, yet desiring to take it and return it—its exertion of force is hard and its burden of responsibility heavy; this is called wisdom, courage, momentum, and strength surpassing the former emperor."
translations.idiomatic: To seize it now instead of mending what still remains unrepaired would tax our strength and our responsibility beyond his—claiming wisdom, courage, and might greater than his."

sentences.zh: 公著悟，竟未能用。

translations.literal: Gong Zhu understood but in the end could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhu saw the point but could not carry the policy.

sentences.zh: 進戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He advanced to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 轍因轉對，言曰：「財賦之原，出於四方，而委於中都。

translations.literal: Zhe by turning memorial audience said: "The springs of fiscal revenue issue from the four quarters and are entrusted to the central capital.
translations.idiomatic: In a routine audience Zhe said, "Revenue springs from the provinces and pools in the capital.

sentences.zh: 故善為國者，藏之於民，其次藏之州郡。

translations.literal: Therefore those skilled in governing a state store it in the people; next store it in prefectures and circuits.
translations.idiomatic: A wise state first hoards wealth among the people, next among the circuits.

sentences.zh: 州郡有餘，則轉運司常足；

translations.literal: When circuits have surplus then the transport commissioner is always full;
translations.idiomatic: When circuits are plentiful the transport offices stay flush;

sentences.zh: 轉運司既足，則戶部不困。

translations.literal: when the transport commissioner is already full then the Revenue Ministry is not distressed.
translations.idiomatic: when transport offices are flush the Revenue Ministry is not straitened.

sentences.zh: 唐制，天下賦稅，其一上供，其一送使，其一留州。

translations.literal: Tang's system: all under Heaven's tax levies, one part presented for the court, one part sent to commissioners, one part retained in the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang the empire's taxes were divided in three: one portion for the throne, one for commissioners, one retained in each prefecture.

sentences.zh: 比之於今，上供之數可謂少矣。

translations.literal: Compared to today, the presented-for-court portion can be called small.
translations.idiomatic: Beside today's practice the court's share was modest indeed.

sentences.zh: 然每有緩急，王命一出，舟車相銜，大事以濟。

translations.literal: Yet whenever there was urgency, once the royal command issued, boats and carts linked in succession and great affairs were accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever crisis came, a single imperial order set boats and carts rolling in chain, and great undertakings were carried through.

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，法制雖殊，而諸道蓄藏之計，猶極豐厚。

translations.literal: Since the ancestors, though institutions differed, the plan of storing reserves in the circuits was still extremely ample.
translations.idiomatic: Under successive emperors the laws changed, but the policy of keeping rich reserves in the circuits remained lavish.

sentences.zh: 是以斂散及時，縱舍由己，利柄所在，所為必成。

translations.literal: Therefore gathering and dispersing were timely, loosening and tightening were in one's own hands; where the profit-handle lay, what was done was sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue could be gathered or released in season, tightened or eased at will; whoever held the fiscal lever could make policy work.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧以來，言利之臣，不知本末之術，欲求富國，而先困轉運司。

translations.literal: Since Xining, the profit-speaking ministers, not knowing the art of root and branch, wished to enrich the state yet first distressed the transport commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xining reforms, profit-minded ministers who did not grasp root-and-branch finance sought to enrich the state by first strangling the transport offices.

sentences.zh: 轉運司既困，則上供不繼；

translations.literal: Once the transport commissioners were distressed, then presentation to the court did not continue;
translations.idiomatic: Once transport offices were drained, tribute to the capital faltered;

sentences.zh: 上供不繼，而戶部亦憊矣。

translations.literal: when presentation to the court did not continue, the Revenue Ministry was also exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: and when tribute faltered the Revenue Ministry itself was worn out.

sentences.zh: 兩司既困，故內帑別藏，雖積如丘山，而委為朽壤，無益於算也。」

translations.literal: Both offices being distressed, therefore the inner treasury's separate stores, though piled like hills, were left as rotten soil and were of no benefit to reckoning."
translations.idiomatic: With both offices crippled, the inner treasury's separate hoards might pile like hills yet rotted unused and did not enter the accounts."

sentences.zh: 尋又言：

translations.literal: Shortly after he again said:
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say:

sentences.zh: 「臣以祖宗故事考之，今日本部所行，體例不同，利害相遠，宜隨事措置，以塞弊原。

translations.literal: " Your subject, examining by the ancestors' precedents, finds what this ministry practices today differs in form, and benefit and harm are far apart; one should dispose matters as they arise to stop the springs of abuse.
translations.idiomatic: " Comparing our ancestors' practice with this ministry's work today, the forms differ and the harms are grave; affairs should be adjusted case by case to choke off abuse at the source.

sentences.zh: 謹具三弊以聞：其一曰分河渠案以為都水監，其二曰分胄案以為軍器監，其三曰分修造案以為將作監。

translations.literal: Respectfully I set forth three abuses to report: the first is dividing the River Works desk to make the Directorate of Water Control; the second is dividing the Armor desk to make the Directorate of Armaments; the third is dividing the Construction desk to make the Directorate of Imperial Works.
translations.idiomatic: I submit three abuses for the throne: first, splitting the River Works desk into the Directorate of Water Control; second, splitting the Armor desk into the Directorate of Armaments; third, splitting the Construction desk into the Directorate of Imperial Works.

sentences.zh: 三監皆隸工部，則本部所專，其餘無幾，出納損益，制在他司。

translations.literal: All three directorates are subordinate to the Ministry of Works, so what this ministry alone controls is little else; disbursement, receipt, loss, and gain are decided in other offices.
translations.idiomatic: All three answer to the Ministry of Works, leaving this ministry almost nothing; disbursement, receipts, and profit and loss are ruled elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 頃者，司馬光秉政，知其為害，嘗使本部收攬諸司利權。

translations.literal: Not long ago Sima Guang held power, knew this was harmful, and once had this ministry gather in the profit-powers of the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang was in power he saw the harm and once ordered this ministry to reclaim fiscal authority from the other agencies.

sentences.zh: 當時所收，不得其要，至今三案猶為他司所擅，深可惜也。

translations.literal: What was gathered then did not get the essentials; to this day the three desks are still usurped by other offices—a deep pity.
translations.idiomatic: The recovery missed the point; to this day the three desks remain in other hands—a great waste.

sentences.zh: 蓋國之有財，猶人之有飲食。

translations.literal: For a state to have wealth is like a person to have food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: A state's wealth is like a person's food and drink.

sentences.zh: 飲食之道，當使口司出納，而腹制多寡。

translations.literal: In the way of food and drink, the mouth should manage disbursement and receipt while the belly controls more or less.
translations.idiomatic: The mouth should take in and pass food while the belly decides how much is enough.

sentences.zh: 然後分佈氣血，以養百骸，耳目賴之以為聰明，手足賴之以為力。

translations.literal: Only then is qi and blood distributed to nourish the hundred bones; ears and eyes rely on it for keenness, hands and feet rely on it for strength.
translations.idiomatic: Only then does nourishment spread through the body; sight and hearing grow keen, hands and feet gain strength.

sentences.zh: 若不專任口腹，而使手足、耳目得分治之，則雖欲求一飽不可得矣，而況于安且壽乎！

translations.literal: If one does not exclusively entrust mouth and belly but lets hands, feet, ears, and eyes each govern in part, then even wishing one full meal cannot be obtained—how much less peace and long life!
translations.idiomatic: If hands, feet, eyes, and ears each fed themselves instead of the mouth and belly, one could not even get a single meal—how then health and long life?

sentences.zh: 今戶部之在朝廷，猶口腹也，而使他司分治其事，何以異此？

translations.literal: Now the Revenue Ministry at court is like mouth and belly, yet other offices are made to divide and govern its affairs—how is this different?
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Ministry at court is the mouth and belly, yet other agencies divide its work—how is that different?

sentences.zh: 自數十年以來，群臣每因一事不舉，輒入建他司。

translations.literal: For several decades, whenever ministers because one matter did not succeed would enter court proposing another office.
translations.idiomatic: For decades, whenever some task failed ministers proposed yet another new agency.

sentences.zh: 利權一分，用財無藝。

translations.literal: Once profit-power is divided, spending funds has no art.
translations.idiomatic: Once fiscal power is split, spending knows no discipline.

sentences.zh: 他司以辦事為效，則不恤財之有無；

translations.literal: Other offices take accomplishing affairs as their effect and do not care whether funds exist or not;
translations.idiomatic: Other agencies prize getting tasks done and ignore whether money exists;

sentences.zh: 戶部以給財為功，則不問事之當否。

translations.literal: the Revenue Ministry takes supplying funds as merit and does not ask whether affairs are fitting or not.
translations.idiomatic: the Revenue Ministry prides itself on paying bills and does not ask whether the tasks are right.

sentences.zh: 彼此各營一職，其勢不復相知，雖使戶部得材智之臣，終亦無益，能否同病，府庫卒空。

translations.literal: Each side pursues one duty; the momentum no longer knows the other. Even if the Revenue Ministry obtained talented and wise ministers, in the end it would still be useless; able and unable share the same illness, and the treasury storehouses end empty.
translations.idiomatic: Each side minds only its own brief; they no longer understand one another. Even talented ministers in the Revenue Ministry could not help; talent and mediocrity share the same disease, and the treasuries end empty.

sentences.zh: 今不早救，後患必甚。

translations.literal: If not rescued early now, later harm will surely be severe.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not remedy this soon, the later harm will be grave.

sentences.zh: 昔嘉祐中，京師頻歲大水，大臣始取河渠案置都水監。

translations.literal: Formerly in Jiayou the capital had flood years in succession; great ministers first took the River Works desk to establish the Directorate of Water Control.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou, after repeated floods in the capital, ministers split off the River Works desk to create the Directorate of Water Control.

sentences.zh: 置監以來，比之舊案，所補何事？

translations.literal: Since establishing the directorate, compared with the old desk, what has it supplemented?
translations.idiomatic: Since the directorate was created, what has it added compared with the old desk?

sentences.zh: 而大不便者，河北有外監丞，侵奪轉運司職事。

translations.literal: What is greatly inconvenient is that in Hebei there is an external supervising assistant who usurps the transport commissioner's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, Hebei has an external supervising assistant who seizes the transport commissioner's duties.

sentences.zh: 轉運司之領河事也，郡之諸埽，埽之吏兵、儲蓄，無事則分，有事則合。

translations.literal: When the transport commissioner led river affairs, the various embankment posts of the prefecture, the clerks, soldiers, and stores of the posts—in peace were divided, in trouble were united.
translations.idiomatic: When transport commissioners led river work, embankment posts in each prefecture kept their own clerks, troops, and stores in peace and pooled them in crisis.

sentences.zh: 水之所向，諸埽趨之，吏兵得以並功，儲蓄得以並用。

translations.literal: Where the water turned, all posts hurried there; clerks and soldiers could combine effort, stores could be used together.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the flood turned, every post rushed there; labor and supplies could be combined.

sentences.zh: 故事作之日，無暴斂傷財之患，事定之後，徐補其闕，兩無所妨。

translations.literal: By the old story on the day of work there was no harm of violent collection injuring wealth; after affairs settled, slowly they made up the gaps—both without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old practice there was no sudden levy that ruined finances; after the crisis, gaps were filled slowly—neither approach blocked the other.

sentences.zh: 自有監丞，據法責成，緩急之際，諸埽不相為用，而轉運司不勝其弊矣。

translations.literal: Once there was a supervising assistant who by law held responsible completion, in moments of urgency the embankment posts did not aid one another, and the transport commissioner could not bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Once supervising assistants enforced the statutes by rote, posts no longer cooperated in emergencies, and transport commissioners were overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 此工部都水監為戶部之害，一也。

translations.literal: This is the harm of the Ministry of Works' Directorate of Water Control to the Revenue Ministry—the first.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first harm the Ministry of Works' Directorate of Water Control does to the Revenue Ministry.

sentences.zh: 先帝一新官制，並建六曹，隨曹付事，故三司故事多隸工曹，名雖近正而實非利。

translations.literal: The former emperor renewed the official system and together established the six ministries, assigning affairs with each ministry; therefore many Three Bureaus precedents were subordinated to the Works ministry—the name though near correctness was in fact not profitable.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor reorganized government into six ministries, and many old Three Bureaus duties were placed under Works—correct in name but harmful in fact.

sentences.zh: 昔胄案所掌，今內為軍器監而上隸工部，外為都作院而上隸提刑司，欲有興作，戶部不得與議。

translations.literal: What the Armor desk once managed is now within as the Armaments Directorate subordinate above to Works, without as the Chief Works Court subordinate above to the Judicial Intendant; if one wishes construction, the Revenue Ministry may not join deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: What the Armor desk once ran is now the Armaments Directorate under Works within and the Chief Works Court under the Judicial Intendant without—so the Revenue Ministry cannot even discuss new projects.

sentences.zh: 訪聞河北道近歲為羊渾脫，動以千計。

translations.literal: Inquiry hears that in recent years the Hebei circuit has made sheep-skin rafts, often to the count of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in Hebei in recent years they have been making inflated sheepskin rafts by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 渾脫之用，必軍行乏水，過渡無船，然後須之。

translations.literal: The use of inflated rafts must be when the army march lacks water and crossing has no boats—only then are they needed.
translations.idiomatic: Such rafts are needed only when troops lack water on the march and must cross a river without boats.

sentences.zh: 而其為物，稍經歲月，必至蠹敗。

translations.literal: Yet as objects, after a little time they necessarily reach rot and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after a few months they inevitably rot away.

sentences.zh: 朝廷無出兵之計，而有司營戢，不顧利害，至使公私應副，虧財害物。

translations.literal: The court has no plan to send troops, yet the responsible offices manage and store without regard to benefit and harm, until public and private must respond and supply, losing wealth and injuring goods.
translations.idiomatic: The court has no campaign planned, yet agencies stockpile them heedless of cost until public and private purses are drained and goods wasted.

sentences.zh: 若專在轉運司，必不至此。

translations.literal: If this were solely in the transport commissioner, it would surely not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: Had this remained with transport commissioners, it would never have come to this.

sentences.zh: 此工部都作院為戶部之害，二也。

translations.literal: This is the harm of the Ministry of Works' Chief Works Court to the Revenue Ministry—the second.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second harm the Ministry of Works' Chief Works Court does to the Revenue Ministry.

sentences.zh: 昔修造案掌百工之事，事有緩急，物有利害，皆得專之。

translations.literal: Formerly the Construction desk managed the hundred crafts' affairs; affairs had urgency and ease, goods had benefit and harm—all could be decided by it alone.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Construction desk ran all public works and could judge urgency, cost, and benefit on its own.

sentences.zh: 今工部以辦職為事，則緩急利害，誰當議之？

translations.literal: Now the Ministry of Works takes accomplishing duties as affairs—then who should deliberate urgency, ease, benefit, and harm?
translations.idiomatic: Now the Ministry of Works only executes tasks—who is to weigh urgency, cost, and benefit?

sentences.zh: 朝廷近以箔場竹箔，積久損爛，創令出賣，上下皆以為當。

translations.literal: The court recently because bamboo screens at the foil yard, long piled, were damaged and rotten, newly ordered them sold; above and below all thought it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The court recently ordered sale of rotting bamboo screens stockpiled at the foil yard, and everyone agreed it was right.

sentences.zh: 指揮未幾，復以諸處營造，歲有科制，遂令般運堆積，以破出賣之計。

translations.literal: The order had not long passed when again because of construction everywhere there were yearly apportionments, and they ordered transport and piling, breaking the plan to sell.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the order gone out when construction quotas everywhere required fresh transport and stockpiling, undoing the sale plan.

sentences.zh: 臣不知將作見工幾何，一歲所用幾何？

translations.literal: Your subject does not know how much work the Imperial Works Directorate sees, how much is used in one year?
translations.idiomatic: I do not know how much work the Imperial Works Directorate actually has, or what it spends in a year.

sentences.zh: 取此積彼，未用之間，有無損敗，而遂為此計。

translations.literal: Taking this and piling that, in the interval before use whether there is loss and ruin—and yet they made this plan.
translations.idiomatic: They take from one stockpile to heap another, where goods may rot unused—and still pursue this scheme.

sentences.zh: 本部雖知不便，而以工部之事，不敢復言。

translations.literal: This ministry though knowing it inconvenient, because it is the Ministry of Works' affair, dares not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: This ministry knows the policy is wrong but, because it is Works' affair, dares not object again.

sentences.zh: 此工部將作監為戶部之害，三也。

translations.literal: This is the harm of the Ministry of Works' Imperial Works Directorate to the Revenue Ministry—the third.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third harm the Ministry of Works' Imperial Works Directorate does to the Revenue Ministry.

sentences.zh: 凡事之類此者多矣，臣不能遍舉也。

translations.literal: Affairs like this are many; your subject cannot enumerate them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cases like these are countless; I cannot list them all.

sentences.zh: 故願明詔有司，罷外水監丞，舉河北河事及諸路都作院皆歸轉運司，至於都水、軍器、將作三監，皆兼隸戶部，使定其事之可否，裁其費之多少，而工部任其功之良苦，程其作之遲速。

translations.literal: Therefore I wish a clear edict to the offices: abolish the external water supervising assistant; entirely return Hebei river affairs and the Chief Works Courts of all circuits to the transport commissioner; as for the three directorates of Water Control, Armaments, and Imperial Works, all should also be subordinate to the Revenue Ministry, letting it decide whether affairs are permissible, cut how much expense, while the Ministry of Works bears the toil of achievement good or bitter and schedules the speed of work.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ask a clear edict: abolish the external water supervising assistant; return Hebei river work and every circuit's Chief Works Court to transport commissioners; and place the three directorates under the Revenue Ministry as well, to decide whether projects are warranted and how much they cost, while Works judges quality of labor and pace of construction.

sentences.zh: 苟可否、多少在戶部，則傷財害民，戶部無所逃其責矣。

translations.literal: If permissibility and amount lie in the Revenue Ministry, then injuring wealth and harming the people—the Revenue Ministry has nowhere to escape its blame.
translations.idiomatic: If the Revenue Ministry decides what is allowed and how much is spent, it cannot escape blame when funds injure the people.

sentences.zh: 苟良苦、遲速在工部，則敗事乏用，工部無所辭其譴矣。

translations.literal: If toil good or bitter and speed or slowness lie in the Ministry of Works, then failing affairs and lacking use—the Ministry of Works has nowhere to decline its reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: If Works judges labor quality and pace, it cannot evade censure when projects fail or funds run short.

sentences.zh: 制出於一，而後天下貧富，可責之戶部矣。」

translations.literal: When regulation issues from one, afterward the empire's poverty and wealth can be charged to the Revenue Ministry."
translations.idiomatic: With policy unified, the empire's wealth or poverty can be laid at the Revenue Ministry's door."

sentences.zh: 哲宗從之，惟都水仍舊。

translations.literal: Zhezong followed it; only Water Control remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong accepted this, except that Water Control stayed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以吏部元豐所定吏額，比舊額數倍，命轍量事裁減。

translations.literal: The court because the Personnel Ministry's Yuanfeng fixed clerk quotas were several times the old quotas ordered Zhe to measure affairs and cut and reduce.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuanfeng clerk quotas set by the Personnel Ministry were several times the old figures, the court ordered Zhe to trim them according to need.

sentences.zh: 吏有白中孚曰：「吏額不難定也。

translations.literal: A clerk reported to Zhongfu: "Clerk quotas are not hard to fix.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk told Zhongfu, "Clerk quotas are not hard to fix.

sentences.zh: 昔之流內銓，今侍郎左選也，事之煩劇，莫過此矣。

translations.literal: Formerly the Inner Flow Selection, now the Vice Minister's Left Selection—of affairs' trouble and weight none surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: The old Inner Flow Selection is now the Vice Minister's Left Selection desk—no office is busier.

sentences.zh: 昔銓吏止十數，而今左選吏至數十，事不加舊而用吏至數倍，何也？

translations.literal: Formerly selection clerks were only a dozen or so, yet now Left Selection clerks reach several tens; affairs do not increase over the old yet clerks used reach several times—why?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a dozen selection clerks sufficed; now the Left Selection employs dozens though the work has not grown—why?

sentences.zh: 昔無重法、重祿，吏通賕賂，則不欲人多以分所得。

translations.literal: Formerly without heavy law and heavy salary, clerks communicated bribes and did not want many people to divide what was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, without strict law or generous salary, clerks took bribes and did not want many mouths to share the take.

sentences.zh: 今行重法，給重祿，賕賂比舊為少，則不忌人多而幸於少事。

translations.literal: Now heavy law is practiced and heavy salary given; bribes compared with the old are fewer, so they do not fear many people and rejoice in few affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now with strict law and generous pay, bribes are fewer, so they welcome more clerks and fewer duties per man.

sentences.zh: 此吏額多少之大情也。

translations.literal: This is the great circumstance of how many or few clerk quotas are.
translations.idiomatic: That is the main reason quotas swell or shrink.

sentences.zh: 舊法，日生事以難易分七等，重者至一分，輕者至一厘以下，積若干分而為一人。

translations.literal: By the old law, daily affairs were divided into seven grades by difficulty; heavy reached one fen, light reached one li or below; accumulating so many fen made one person.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old law daily tasks were graded in seven levels of difficulty, from one fen down to a li or less, and enough points made one clerk's workload.

sentences.zh: 今若取逐司兩月事定其分數，則吏額多少之限，無所逃矣。」

translations.literal: Now if one takes each office's two months of affairs to fix their points, then the limit of how many or few clerk quotas—there is nowhere to escape."
translations.idiomatic: If we score each office's work over two months, the proper quota could not be evaded."

sentences.zh: 轍曰：「此群吏身計所係也。

translations.literal: Zhe said: "This concerns the body-livelihood of the mass of clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "That touches every clerk's livelihood.

sentences.zh: 若以分數為人數，必大有所損，將大致紛訴，雖朝廷亦不能守。」

translations.literal: If by points one fixes headcount, there will surely be great loss; they will largely raise disputes in complaint—even the court also cannot maintain it."
translations.idiomatic: If headcount were set strictly by points, many would suffer and appeal in uproar—even the court could not hold the line."

sentences.zh: 乃具以白宰執，請據實立額，俟吏之年滿轉出，或事故死亡者勿補，及額而止。

translations.literal: He then fully reported to the chief ministers, asking to establish quotas according to reality, waiting until clerks' years were full and they transferred out, or on accident or death not to replenish, and stop when quota was reached.
translations.idiomatic: He reported fully to the chief ministers, proposing realistic quotas: when clerks completed their terms or died, do not refill posts until the quota was met.

sentences.zh: 不過十年，羨額當盡。

translations.literal: Within no more than ten years the surplus quota should be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years the surplus would be gone.

sentences.zh: 功雖稍緩，而見吏知非身患，不復怨矣。

translations.literal: The achievement though slightly slow, yet when clerks saw it was not their body's suffering they no longer resented.
translations.idiomatic: Progress would be slower, but clerks would see they were not singled out for harm and would cease to resent it.

sentences.zh: 呂大防命諸司吏任永壽與省吏數人典之，遂背轍議以立額，日裁損吏員，復以好惡改易諸局次。

translations.literal: Lü Dafang ordered office clerk Ren Yongshou and several capital clerks to oversee it; they then went against Zhe's deliberation to establish quotas, daily cutting clerk numbers, and again by likes and dislikes changed the order of various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafang put office clerk Ren Yongshou and several capital clerks in charge; they defied Zhe's plan, cut staff daily, and rearranged bureau rankings by favor.

sentences.zh: 永壽復以贓刺配，大防略依轍議行之。

translations.literal: Yongshou again because of embezzlement was tattooed and exiled; Dafang roughly followed Zhe's deliberation in practicing it.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou was tattooed and exiled for embezzlement; Dafang then roughly followed Zhe's approach.

sentences.zh: 代軾為翰林學士，尋權吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He replaced Shi as Hanlin Academician; shortly after he acted as Personnel Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Shi as Hanlin Academician and soon acted as Personnel Minister.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，館客者侍讀學士王師儒能誦洵、軾之文及轍《茯苓賦》，恨不得見全集。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Khitan, the host-guest was Attendant Reader Academician Wang Shiru, who could recite Xun's and Shi's writings and Zhe's "Fu on Poria," and regretted he could not see the complete collection.
translations.idiomatic: On mission to Khitan, his host Wang Shiru, Attendant Reader Academician, could recite Xun's and Shi's works and Zhe's "Fu on Poria," and lamented he could not see their full collected writings.

sentences.zh: 使還，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 自元祐初，一新庶政，至是五年矣。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Yuanyou a general renewal of common government—by now it had been five years.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanyou began the government had been broadly renewed; five years had now passed.

sentences.zh: 人心已定，惟元豐舊黨分佈中外，多起邪說以搖撼在位，呂大防、劉摯患之，欲稍引用，以平夙怨，謂之「調停」。

translations.literal: People's hearts were already settled; only the Yuanfeng old faction was distributed within and without, often raising perverse talk to shake those in office. Lü Dafang and Liu Zhi were troubled by it and wished slightly to employ them to level old resentments—calling it "mediation."
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion had settled, but Yuanfeng loyalists still spread inside and outside court, spreading seditious talk to shake those in power. Lü Dafang and Liu Zhi, troubled by this, wished to bring some back to soothe old grudges—calling it "mediation."

sentences.zh: 宣仁后疑不決，轍面斥其非，復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren doubted and did not decide; Zhe to her face denounced its wrongness and again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren hesitated; Zhe rebuked the plan to her face and submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 「臣近面論，君子小人不可並處，聖意似不以臣言為非者。

translations.literal: " Your subject recently argued in person that gentlemen and petty men cannot dwell together; the sage intent seems not to take your subject's words as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " I recently argued in audience that gentlemen and petty men cannot serve together, and Your Majesty did not seem to reject me.

sentences.zh: 然天威咫尺，言詞迫遽，有所不盡，臣而不言，誰當救其失者！

translations.literal: Yet heaven's majesty is within a foot; words were pressed and hurried—something was not complete. If your subject does not speak, who should rescue its error!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Your Majesty's awful presence my words were hurried and incomplete. If I do not speak now, who will correct the error?

sentences.zh: 親君子，遠小人，則主尊國安；

translations.literal: Draw near gentlemen, keep petty men distant—then the ruler is honored and the state secure;
translations.idiomatic: Honor gentlemen and keep petty men at a distance, and the ruler is exalted and the state secure;

sentences.zh: 疏君子，任小人，則主憂國殆。

translations.literal: keep gentlemen distant, employ petty men—then the ruler is troubled and the state endangered.
translations.idiomatic: keep gentlemen distant and employ petty men, and the ruler is troubled and the state endangered.

sentences.zh: 此理之必然。

translations.literal: This is the necessity of principle.
translations.idiomatic: That is an iron law of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 未聞以小人在外，憂其不悅而引之於內，以自遺患也。

translations.literal: One has not heard of petty men outside, fearing they are displeased and drawing them within, to bequeath trouble to oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has a ruler, fearing discontent among petty men outside, invited them within and courted disaster.

sentences.zh: 故臣謂小人雖不可任以腹心，至於牧守四方，奔走庶務，無所偏廢可也。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject says petty men though cannot be entrusted with the heart's center, as to governing and guarding the four quarters and running to common affairs, none need be wholly discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men must not be trusted at the center, yet in prefectures and routine duties they need not all be excluded.

sentences.zh: 若遂引之於內，是猶患盜賊之欲得財，而導之於寢室，知虎豹之欲食肉，而開之以坰牧，無是理也。

translations.literal: If one then draws them within, this is like worrying that robbers wish to obtain wealth and guiding them to the bedchamber, knowing tigers and leopards wish to eat flesh and opening the outer pasture to them—there is no such principle.
translations.idiomatic: To bring them inside is like leading thieves to the bedchamber because they want money, or opening the pasture gate to tigers because they hunger for meat—there is no sense in it.

sentences.zh: 且君子小人，勢同冰炭，同處必爭。

translations.literal: Moreover gentlemen and petty men—their momentum is like ice and charcoal; dwelling together they must contend.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen and petty men are as incompatible as ice and fire; put them together and they must fight.

sentences.zh: 一爭之後，小人必勝，君子必敗。

translations.literal: After one contention petty men surely win, gentlemen surely lose.
translations.idiomatic: Once they contend, petty men always win and gentlemen always lose.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 小人貪利忍恥，擊之則難去，君子潔身重義，沮之則引退。

translations.literal: Petty men are greedy for profit and endure shame; strike them and they are hard to remove. Gentlemen keep the body pure and value righteousness; discourage them and they withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men crave profit and swallow shame; strike them and they cling. Gentlemen prize integrity; discourage them and they withdraw.

sentences.zh: 古語曰：「一薰一蕕，十年尚猶有臭。」

translations.literal: An old saying says: "One fragrant herb, one foul herb—after ten years there is still odor."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "One fragrant plant and one foul—after ten years the stench remains."

sentences.zh: 蓋謂此矣。

translations.literal: This is what it speaks of.
translations.idiomatic: That proverb means exactly this.

sentences.zh: 先帝聰明聖智，疾頹靡之俗，將以綱紀四方，比靈斯三代。

translations.literal: The former emperor was intelligent and sage-wise, hated the decadent custom, and wished by regulation to order the four quarters, comparing spirit with the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was wise and sage; he hated slack custom and meant to bring order to the realm and rival the Three Dynasties in spirit.

sentences.zh: 而臣下不能將順，造作諸法，上逆天意，下失民心。

translations.literal: Yet ministers could not lead and follow; they fabricated various laws, above opposing heaven's intent, below losing the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his ministers could not follow his lead; they invented laws that defied heaven's intent above and lost the people's hearts below.

sentences.zh: 二聖因民所願，取而更之，上下忻慰。

translations.literal: The two sages followed what the people wished, took and changed them; above and below were pleased and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: The two sage rulers changed policy as the people wished, and court and country rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 則前者用事之臣，今朝廷雖不加斥逐，其勢亦不能復留矣。

translations.literal: Then the former ministers who held power—though the court today does not add dismissal and expulsion, by momentum they also cannot remain.
translations.idiomatic: Those who once held power cannot remain even if the court does not formally expel them.

sentences.zh: 尚賴二聖慈仁，宥之于外，蓋已厚矣。

translations.literal: Still relying on the two sages' kindness and benevolence to pardon them outside—this is already generous.
translations.idiomatic: That the two sage rulers have spared them outside court is already generous enough.

sentences.zh: 而議者惑於說，乃欲招而納之，與之共事，謂之「調停」。

translations.literal: Yet deliberators, confused by talk, then wish to summon and admit them, work affairs together with them—calling it "mediation."
translations.idiomatic: Yet some counselors, misled by rumor, wish to summon them in and work with them—calling it "mediation."

sentences.zh: 非輩若返，豈肯但已哉？

translations.literal: If that faction returns, how would they be willing merely to stop?
translations.idiomatic: If that faction returns, will they simply stop there?

sentences.zh: 必將戕害正人，漸復舊事，以快私忿。

translations.literal: They will surely harm upright men, gradually restore old affairs, to satisfy private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely harm upright men, gradually restore the old order, and satisfy private grudges.

sentences.zh: 人臣被禍，蓋不足言，臣所惜者，祖宗朝廷也。

translations.literal: Ministers suffering calamity is perhaps not worth speaking of; what your subject regrets is the ancestral court.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers may suffer—that is not my concern; what I grieve for is the ancestral court.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下斷自聖心，勿為流言所惑，勿使小人一進，後有噬臍之悔，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Only beg Your Majesty to decide from the sage heart, not be confused by floating talk, not let petty men advance one step—afterward there will be the regret of biting the navel—then All under Heaven will be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide from your own sage judgment, not be swayed by rumor, and not let petty men advance one step—for if you do, you will bite your navel in regret, and the empire will be blessed."

sentences.zh: 疏入，宣仁后命宰執讀於簾前，曰：「轍疑吾君臣兼用邪正，其言極中理。」

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Empress Dowager Xuanren ordered the chief ministers to read it before the curtain and said: "Zhe suspects that we ruler and ministers employ both the crooked and the upright together—his words extremely hit the principle."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Empress Dowager Xuanren had the chief ministers read it before the curtain and said, "Zhe suspects we mean to employ both upright men and petty men together—his argument is exactly right."

sentences.zh: 諸臣從而和之，「調停」之說遂已。

translations.literal: The various ministers followed and harmonized; the talk of "mediation" thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers agreed, and the "mediation" proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 轍又奏曰：

translations.literal: Zhe again memorialized saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhe submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 「竊見方今天下雖未大治，而祖宗綱紀具在，州郡民物粗安。

translations.literal: " Your subject ventures to see that though All under Heaven today is not greatly ordered, yet the ancestors' regulations and discipline are complete, and in prefectures and circuits the people and goods are roughly secure.
translations.idiomatic: " I observe that though the realm is not yet fully well governed, the ancestral institutions remain intact and the provinces are roughly at peace.

sentences.zh: 若大臣正己平心，無生事要功之意，因弊修法，為安民靖國之術，則人心自定，雖有異黨，誰不歸心？

translations.literal: If great ministers correct themselves and level their hearts, without intent to stir affairs and demand merit, and following abuses repair law as the art of settling the people and quieting the state, then people's hearts will themselves settle; though there be rival factions, who will not turn their hearts?
translations.idiomatic: If ministers discipline themselves, level their hearts, and cease stirring up trouble for merit; if they mend what is broken and govern to settle the people and quiet the state—then hearts will settle of themselves, and who among rival factions would not turn loyal?

sentences.zh: 向者異同反覆之心，蓋亦不足慮矣。

translations.literal: The former hearts of difference and sameness, reversal and return—probably also are not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: The old fears of factional reversal would scarcely matter.

sentences.zh: 但患朝廷舉事，類不審詳，曩者，黃河北流，正得水性，而水官穿鑿，欲導之使東，移下就高，汩五行之理。

translations.literal: Only the worry is that when the court undertakes affairs it mostly is not careful and detailed. Formerly the Yellow River flowed north—this truly obtained water's nature—yet water officials bored and cut, wishing to guide it to go east, moving low to high, muddying the principle of the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: My worry is that the court often acts without thorough deliberation. The Yellow River once flowed north as water's nature required, yet hydraulic officials bored channels to force it east, lifting low water uphill and violating the natural order.

sentences.zh: 及陛下遣使按視，知不可為，猶或固執不從。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty sent envoys to inspect on the spot and knew it could not be done, some still obstinately would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Your Majesty sent inspectors and saw it could not be done, some still stubbornly refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 經今累歲，回河雖罷，減水尚存，遂使河朔生靈，財力俱困。

translations.literal: Through accumulated years to now, though returning the river was stopped, water-reduction works still remain, until the living souls of the Hebei north, wealth and strength, are both distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Years have passed; though the forced return was abandoned, drainage works remain, and the people of Hebei are exhausted in purse and strength.

sentences.zh: 今者西夏、青唐，外皆臣順，朝廷招來之厚，惟恐失之。

translations.literal: Now Western Xia and Qingtang without all submit as subjects; the court's summoning and coming is generous—only fearing to lose them.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xia and Qingtang now submit abroad, and the court courts them lavishly, fearing only to lose their allegiance.

sentences.zh: 而熙河將吏創築二堡，以侵其膏腴，議納醇忠，以奪其節鉞，功未可覬，爭已先形。

translations.literal: Yet Xihe generals and clerks newly built two forts to invade their fertile lands, deliberated receiving Chunzhong to seize his command tally and axe—merit not yet to be glimpsed, contention already first formed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xihe officers newly built two forts on their fertile lands, plotted to install Zhao Chunzhong and seize his command—before any gain could be hoped for, quarrel had already broken out.

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖知其非，終不明白處置，若遂養成邊釁，關陝豈復安居？

translations.literal: The court though knew it was wrong, in the end did not clearly understand how to dispose; if this then nourishes frontier quarrel, can Guan and Shaan again dwell in peace?
translations.idiomatic: The court knew this was wrong yet never settled it clearly; if border strife is thus nurtured, can Guanzhong and Shaanxi know peace again?

sentences.zh: 如此二事，則臣所謂宜正己平心，無生事要功者也。

translations.literal: Such two affairs are what your subject calls fitting to correct oneself and level the heart, without stirring affairs to demand merit.
translations.idiomatic: These two cases are what I mean by ministers correcting themselves and ceasing to stir trouble for merit.

sentences.zh: 昔嘉祐以前，鄉差衙前，民間常有破產之患。

translations.literal: Formerly before Jiayou, rural corvée for yamen runners—among the people there was often the affliction of ruined households.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jiayou, rural corvée for yamen runners often ruined households.

sentences.zh: 熙寧以後，出賣坊場以雇衙前，民間不復知有衙前之苦。

translations.literal: After Xining they sold market stalls to hire yamen runners; among the people they no longer knew the suffering of yamen runners.
translations.idiomatic: After Xining, market-stall fees hired runners, and the people forgot yamen-runner hardship.

sentences.zh: 及元祐之初，務於復舊，一例復差。

translations.literal: When Yuanyou began they strove to restore the old, uniformly restoring corvée.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanyou the court strove to restore the old ways and uniformly revived corvée.

sentences.zh: 官收坊場之錢，民出衙前之費，四方驚顧，眾議沸騰。

translations.literal: The government collected market-stall money, the people paid yamen-runner expenses; the four quarters looked on in alarm, public discussion boiled.
translations.idiomatic: The state took stall fees while the people paid runner costs; the empire looked on in alarm and public outcry boiled over.

sentences.zh: 尋知不可，旋又復雇。

translations.literal: Soon knowing it could not be done, they then again restored hiring.
translations.idiomatic: They soon saw it would not work and reverted to hired service.

sentences.zh: 去年之秋，又復差法。

translations.literal: Last autumn they again restored the corvée law.
translations.idiomatic: Last autumn corvée was imposed again.

sentences.zh: 又熙寧雇役之法，三等人戶，並出役錢，上戶以家產高強，出錢無藝，下戶昔不充役，亦遣出錢。

translations.literal: Moreover under Xining's hired-service law the three grades of households all paid service money; upper households because household property was high and strong paid money without limit; lower households who formerly did not perform service were also sent to pay money.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xining's hired-service law all three household grades paid service money: the wealthy paid without limit, and poorer households who had never served were also charged.

sentences.zh: 故此二等人戶，不免咨怨。

translations.literal: Therefore these two grades of households could not avoid complaint and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Those two grades naturally complained.

sentences.zh: 至於中等，昔既已自差役，今又出錢不多，雇法之行，最為其便。

translations.literal: As for the middle grade, formerly they already performed corvée themselves; now they also paid not much money—the practice of hired service was most convenient for them.
translations.idiomatic: Middle households had always performed corvée themselves and now paid only modest fees—hired service suited them best.

sentences.zh: 罷行雇法，上下二等，欣躍可知，唯是中等則反為害。

translations.literal: Abolishing hired service—the upper and lower two grades, their joy can be known; only the middle grade then instead suffers harm.
translations.idiomatic: Abolishing hired service plainly delighted the upper and lower grades, but harmed the middle.

sentences.zh: 且如畿縣中等之家，例出役錢三貫，若經十年，為錢三十貫而已。

translations.literal: For example in capital-district counties middle households by rule paid three guan in service money; if over ten years, it was only thirty guan in money.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital districts a middle household paid three guan in service money yearly—only thirty guan over ten years.

sentences.zh: 今差役既行，諸縣手力，最為輕役；

translations.literal: Now that corvée is practiced, in all counties clerk labor is the lightest service;
translations.idiomatic: Under corvée, clerk labor is counted the lightest duty;

sentences.zh: 農民在官，日使百錢，最為輕費。

translations.literal: farmers serving in office at a hundred cash per day is the lightest expense.
translations.idiomatic: a farmer serving in office at a hundred cash a day seems the cheapest rate.

sentences.zh: 然一歲之用，已為三十六貫，二年役滿，為費七十餘貫。

translations.literal: Yet one year's use is already thirty-six guan; when two years' service is full, the expense is more than seventy guan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one year already costs thirty-six guan, and a two-year term costs more than seventy.

sentences.zh: 罷役而歸，寬鄉得閒三年，狹鄉不及一歲。

translations.literal: When service ends and they return, in broad districts they get three years' rest; in narrow districts not even one year.
translations.idiomatic: After service ends, broad districts grant three years' rest; narrow ones less than one.

sentences.zh: 以此較之，則差役五年之費，倍於雇役十年。

translations.literal: Comparing by this, then corvée's expense in five years doubles hired service in ten.
translations.idiomatic: By this reckoning, five years of corvée cost twice ten years of hired service.

sentences.zh: 賦役所出，多在中等。

translations.literal: What tax and service yield comes mostly from the middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: Most tax and service revenue comes from middle households.

sentences.zh: 如此條目，不便非一，故天下皆思雇役而厭差役，今五年矣。

translations.literal: Such items of inconvenience are not one; therefore all under Heaven all think of hired service and dislike corvée—now five years.
translations.idiomatic: Inconveniences like these are many; for five years the empire has longed for hired service and resented corvée.

sentences.zh: 如此二事，則臣所謂宜因弊修法，為安民靖國之術者也。

translations.literal: Such two affairs are what your subject calls fitting to follow abuses and repair law as the art of settling the people and quieting the state.
translations.idiomatic: These two cases are what I mean by mending what is broken to settle the people and quiet the state.

sentences.zh: 臣以聞見淺狹，不能盡知當今得失。

translations.literal: Your subject's hearing and seeing are shallow and narrow; I cannot fully know today's gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: My knowledge is limited and I cannot grasp every present gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 然四事不去，如臣等輩猶知其非，而況于心懷異同，志在反覆，幸國之失，有以藉口者乎？

translations.literal: Yet if these four affairs are not removed, even such as your subject still know their wrongness—how much more those whose hearts harbor difference and sameness, whose aim is reversal, who rejoice in the state's errors and have something to seize as pretext?
translations.idiomatic: Yet if these four abuses remain, even men like me see they are wrong—how much more those who harbor factional hearts, seek reversal, and welcome state failures for a pretext?

sentences.zh: 臣恐如此四事，彼已默識於心，多造謗議，待時而發，以搖撼眾聽矣。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that regarding such four affairs they have already silently recognized them in heart, will much manufacture slander and criticism, wait for the time to issue, and shake the multitude's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I fear they already note these four points in silence, will spread slander, and wait their moment to shake public opinion.

sentences.zh: 伏乞宣諭宰執，事有失當，改之勿疑，法或未完，修之無倦。

translations.literal: Respectfully beg to instruct the chief ministers: where affairs are inappropriate, change them without doubt; where law is not yet complete, repair without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to tell the chief ministers: where policy errs, change it without hesitation; where laws are incomplete, mend them tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 苟民心既得，則異議自消。

translations.literal: If the people's hearts are already obtained, then dissenting talk will itself disappear.
translations.idiomatic: Once the people's hearts are won, dissent will fade of itself.

sentences.zh: 陛下端拱以享承平，大臣逡巡以安富貴，海內蒙福，上下攸同，豈不休哉！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty sits upright with folded hands to enjoy enduring peace; great ministers hesitate and circle to secure wealth and rank; within the seas all receive blessing, above and below alike—how is it not glorious!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may sit at ease in lasting peace, ministers may secure wealth and rank in due course, the realm will be blessed, and court and country alike will rejoice—what glory could exceed this?"

sentences.zh: 大臣恥過，終莫肯改。

translations.literal: Great ministers were ashamed of fault and to the end were unwilling to change.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were too ashamed of error to change.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜尚書右丞，進門下侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and advanced to Vice Minister of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and promoted to Vice Minister of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 初，夏人來賀登極，相繼求和，且議地界。
