translations.literal: At the beginning the Xia people came to congratulate the accession, successively sought peace, and also deliberated the border.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xi Xia came to congratulate the enthronement, then repeatedly sought peace and debated the border.

sentences.zh: 朝廷許約，地界已定，付以歲賜。

translations.literal: The court permitted the treaty; the border was already fixed and yearly gifts were paid.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed to a treaty, fixed the border, and paid the annual gifts.

sentences.zh: 久之，議不決。

translations.literal: After a long time deliberation was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 明年，夏人以兵襲涇原。

translations.literal: The next year the Xia people with troops raided Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xi Xia attacked Jingyuan with troops.

sentences.zh: 殺掠弓箭手數千人，朝廷忍之不問，遣使往賜策命。

translations.literal: They killed and plundered several thousand bowmen; the court endured it without inquiry and sent envoys to bestow patent and command.
translations.idiomatic: They killed and plundered thousands of bowmen; the court swallowed the insult and sent envoys with patents and commands.

sentences.zh: 夏人受禮倨慢，以地界為辭，不復入謝，再犯涇原。

translations.literal: The Xia people received the rites arrogantly and slowly, used the border as pretext, did not again enter to give thanks, and again violated Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xia received the gifts arrogantly, pleaded the border dispute, refused to return thanks, and struck Jingyuan again.

sentences.zh: 四年，來賀坤成節，且議地界。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they came to congratulate the Kuncheng festival and also deliberated the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they came for the Kuncheng festival and again debated the border.

sentences.zh: 朝廷先以歲賜予之，地界又未決。

translations.literal: The court first gave them the yearly gifts, yet the border was again undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The court paid the annual gifts first while the border remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 夏人乃於疆事多方侵求，熙河將佐范育、种誼等，遂背約侵築買孤、勝如二堡，夏人即平蕩之。

translations.literal: The Xia people then on border affairs in many ways pressed demands; Xihe assistants Fan Yu, Chong Yi, and others thereupon broke treaty and invasively built Maigu and Shengru forts; the Xia people immediately leveled them.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xia then pressed many border demands; Fan Yu, Chong Yi, and other Xihe officers broke treaty and built Maigu and Shengru forts, which Xi Xia promptly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 育等又欲以兵納趙醇忠，及擅招其部人千餘，朝廷卻而不受，西邊騷然。

translations.literal: Yu and others also wished with troops to receive Zhao Chunzhong, and on their own summoned more than a thousand of his tribesmen; the court refused and did not accept—the western border was disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and others also wished to install Zhao Chunzhong by force and privately recruited more than a thousand of his tribesmen; the court refused, and the west was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 轍乞罷育、誼，別擇老將以守熙河。

translations.literal: Zhe begged to dismiss Yu and Yi and separately select an old general to guard Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe asked to remove Yu and Yi and appoint a seasoned general to hold Xihe.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后以為然，大臣竟主育、誼，不從。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren thought it so; great ministers in the end upheld Yu and Yi and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren agreed, but the chief ministers backed Yu and Yi and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 轍又面奏：「人君與人臣，事體不同。

translations.literal: Zhe again memorialized in audience: "Ruler and minister—the form of affairs differs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe again argued in audience: "A ruler and a minister face affairs differently.

sentences.zh: 人臣雖明見是非，而力所不加，須至且止；

translations.literal: A minister though clearly sees right and wrong, yet what his strength cannot reach must stop for the time;
translations.idiomatic: A minister may see right and wrong clearly yet, where power cannot reach, must for the moment desist;

sentences.zh: 人君於事，不知則已，知而不能行，則事權去矣。

translations.literal: a ruler regarding affairs—if he does not know, so be it; if he knows yet cannot act, then the power of affairs is gone.
translations.idiomatic: but for a ruler, ignorance is one thing—knowing yet failing to act means authority is lost.

sentences.zh: 臣今言此，蓋欲陛下收攬威柄，以正君臣之分而已。

translations.literal: Your subject now speaks this, intending only that Your Majesty gather in the authority-handle to correct the division between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: I speak thus only to urge Your Majesty to reclaim authority and restore the proper relation between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 若專聽所謂，不以漸制之，及其太甚，必加之罪，不免逐去。

translations.literal: If one exclusively listens to what is said and does not gradually control it, when it becomes too extreme one must add guilt and they cannot avoid being expelled.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty listens only to them and does not restrain them gradually, when excess comes you must punish them and drive them out.

sentences.zh: 事至如此，豈朝廷美事？

translations.literal: When affairs reach this, is it a beautiful affair for the court?
translations.idiomatic: When matters come to that, is it a credit to the court?

sentences.zh: 故臣欲保全大臣，非欲害之也。」

translations.literal: Therefore your subject wishes to preserve great ministers, not to harm them."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to preserve the ministers, not to harm them."

sentences.zh: 六年，熙河奏：「夏人十萬騎壓通遠軍境，挑掘所爭崖巉，殺人三日而退。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Xihe memorialized: "Xia people with a hundred thousand riders pressed the Tongyuan Army border, provoked and dug at the disputed cliff faces, killed people for three days and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Xihe reported: "Xi Xia sent a hundred thousand horsemen against Tongyuan, dug at the disputed cliffs, killed for three days, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乞因其退，急移近裏堡砦於界，乘利而往，不須復守誠信。」

translations.literal: We beg, as they withdraw, urgently to move nearby forts and stockades to the border, take advantage and go forward, not needing again to keep faith and trust."
translations.idiomatic: We ask, while they withdraw, to rush nearby forts to the border, seize the advantage, and abandon good faith."

sentences.zh: 下大臣會議。

translations.literal: It was sent down for great ministers to confer.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 轍曰：「當先定議欲用兵耶，不用耶？」

translations.literal: Zhe said: "One should first fix deliberation—does one wish to use troops or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "We must first decide whether we mean to use troops or not."

sentences.zh: 呂大防曰：「如合用兵，亦不得不用。」

translations.literal: Lü Dafang said: "If troops should be used, one also cannot avoid using them."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafang said, "If troops are needed, we cannot refuse to use them."

sentences.zh: 轍曰：「凡用兵，先論理之曲直。

translations.literal: Zhe said: "In all use of troops, first discuss principle's bent and straight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "In every use of force, right and wrong come first.

sentences.zh: 我若不直，兵決不當用。

translations.literal: If we are not straight, troops absolutely should not be used.
translations.idiomatic: If we are in the wrong, troops must not be used.

sentences.zh: 朝廷須與夏人議地界，欲用慶曆舊例，以彼此見今住處當中為直，此理最簡直。

translations.literal: The court must deliberate the border with the Xia people, wishing to use the Qingli old precedent—taking the middle between where each side now dwells as straight; this principle is most simple and direct.
translations.idiomatic: The court had to negotiate the border with Xi Xia and wished to use the Qingli precedent—drawing the line midway between present holdings—which was the simplest justice.

sentences.zh: 夏人不從，朝廷遂不固執。

translations.literal: The Xia people did not follow; the court thereupon did not obstinately insist.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xia refused, and the court did not insist.

sentences.zh: 蓋朝廷臨事，常患先易後難，此所謂先易者也。

translations.literal: For the court facing affairs often worries first easy, later hard—this is what is called first easy.
translations.idiomatic: The court often takes the easy step first and the hard step later—this was the easy step.

sentences.zh: 既而許於非所賜城砦，依綏州例，以二十里為界，十里為堡鋪，十里為草地。

translations.literal: Afterward they permitted what were not granted forts and stockades; following the Sui Prefecture precedent, twenty li as border, ten li as fort posts, ten li as pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Then they yielded on forts not originally granted, following the Suizhou precedent: twenty li for the border, ten for fort posts, ten for pasture.

sentences.zh: 要約才定，朝廷又要兩砦界首侵夏地，一抹取直，夏人見從。

translations.literal: The compact had just been fixed when the court again demanded the two forts' border heads invade Xia territory, smoothing to take straight—the Xia people saw and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly was the treaty fixed when the court demanded straightening the border at two forts by encroaching on Xi Xia land—and Xi Xia yielded.

sentences.zh: 又要夏界更留草地十里，夏人亦許。

translations.literal: They again demanded the Xia border leave ten more li of pasture; the Xia people also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded ten more li of pasture on the Xi Xia side—and Xi Xia agreed again.

sentences.zh: 凡此所謂後難者也。

translations.literal: All this is what is called later hard.
translations.idiomatic: All this was the hard step that followed.

sentences.zh: 今欲於定西城與隴諾堡一抹取直，所侵夏地凡百數十里。

translations.literal: Now they wish at Dingxi City and Longnuo Fort to smooth and take straight; the Xia territory invaded totals more than a hundred and several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Now they wish to straighten the line between Dingxi City and Longnuo Fort, encroaching more than a hundred li of Xi Xia territory.

sentences.zh: 隴諾祖宗舊疆，豈所謂非所賜城砦耶？

translations.literal: Longnuo is the ancestors' old territory—how is it what is called a not-granted fort and stockade?
translations.idiomatic: Longnuo was ancestral territory—how is it an ungranted fort?

sentences.zh: 此則不直，致寇之大者也。」

translations.literal: This then is not straight—the great matter of bringing invaders."
translations.idiomatic: This is injustice—the greatest cause of inviting enemies."

sentences.zh: 劉摯曰：「不用兵雖美，然事有須用兵者，亦不可不用也。」

translations.literal: Liu Zhi said: "Not using troops though beautiful, yet when affairs require troops one also cannot avoid using them."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi said, "Avoiding war is fine, but when war is necessary it cannot be refused."

sentences.zh: 轍奏曰：「夏兵十萬壓熙河境上，不於他處，專於所爭處殺人、掘崖巉，此意可見，此非西人之罪，皆朝廷不直之故。

translations.literal: Zhe memorialized: "Xia troops a hundred thousand press on the Xihe border; not elsewhere—they specialize at the disputed place in killing people and digging cliff faces. This intent can be seen. This is not the western people's fault; all is because the court is not straight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "A hundred thousand Xi Xia horsemen press Xihe, yet kill and dig only at the disputed cliffs—their intent is plain. This is not Xi Xia's fault but the court's injustice.

sentences.zh: 熙河輒敢生事，不守誠信，臣欲詰責帥臣耳。」

translations.literal: Xihe rashly dares to stir affairs and not keep faith and trust; your subject wishes only to interrogate and blame the frontier commander."
translations.idiomatic: Xihe dares stir trouble and break faith—I mean only to rebuke the frontier commanders."

sentences.zh: 後屢因邊兵深入夏地，宣仁后遂從轍議。

translations.literal: Later, repeatedly because border troops deeply entered Xia territory, Empress Dowager Xuanren thereupon followed Zhe's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as border troops repeatedly raided deep into Xi Xia, Empress Dowager Xuanren followed Zhe's advice.

sentences.zh: 時三省除李清臣吏部尚書，給事中范祖禹封還詔書，且言姚勔亦言之。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Departments appointed Li Qingchen Personnel Minister; Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu sealed and returned the edict document, and said Yao Xun also spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments appointed Li Qingchen Personnel Minister; Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu returned the edict, and Yao Xun had spoken against it as well.

sentences.zh: 三省復除蒲宗孟兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The Three Departments again appointed Pu Zongmeng Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments then appointed Pu Zongmeng Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 轍奏：「前除清臣，給諫紛然，爭之未定。

translations.literal: Zhe memorialized: "The former appointment of Qingchen—the remonstrating and admonishing offices were in uproar; contention was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "Qingchen's earlier appointment stirred the remonstrance offices, and debate had not ended.

sentences.zh: 今又用宗孟，恐不便。」

translations.literal: Now again employing Zongmeng—I fear it is not convenient."
translations.idiomatic: To appoint Zongmeng now would be unwise."

sentences.zh: 宣仁后曰：「奈闕官何？」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "What to do about vacant offices?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren said, "What of the vacant posts?"

sentences.zh: 轍曰：「尚書闕官已數年，何嘗闕事？

translations.literal: Zhe said: "Minister posts have been vacant several years—when did affairs lack?
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said, "Minister posts have stood empty for years—when did government stop for that?

sentences.zh: 今日用此二人，正與去年用鄧溫伯無異。

translations.literal: Today employing these two men is exactly no different from last year employing Deng Wenbo.
translations.idiomatic: Appointing these two today is no different from employing Deng Wenbo last year.

sentences.zh: 此三人者，非有大惡，但昔與王珪、蔡確輩並進，意思與今日聖政不合。

translations.literal: These three men do not have great evil, but formerly they advanced together with Wang Gui, Cai Que, and their kind—their intent does not match today's sage government.
translations.idiomatic: These three are not greatly wicked, but they rose with Wang Gui and Cai Que—their outlook does not fit today's policy.

sentences.zh: 見今尚書共闕四人，若並用似此四人，使黨類互進，恐朝廷自是不安靜矣。」

translations.literal: Now minister posts together lack four men; if all four were employed like these four, letting faction kinds advance one another, I fear the court from itself would no longer be quiet."
translations.idiomatic: Four minister posts are vacant; if all were filled with men like these and factions advanced together, the court would never know peace."

sentences.zh: 議遂止。

translations.literal: Deliberation thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments were dropped.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，哲宗起李清臣為中書舍人，鄧潤甫為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng Zhezong raised Li Qingchen to Secretariat Drafter and Deng Runfu to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng, Zhezong raised Li Qingchen to Secretariat Drafter and Deng Runfu to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二人久在外，不得志，稍復言熙、豐事以激怒哲宗意。

translations.literal: The two men had long been outside and unfulfilled; they slightly again spoke of Xi and Feng affairs to stir Zhezong's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Long out of power and frustrated, they began again to speak of Xining and Yuanfeng reforms to stir Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 會廷試進士，清臣撰策題，即為邪說。

translations.literal: It happened at the court examination of jinshi Qingchen composed the policy topic—it was at once perverse talk.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination Qingchen composed the policy topic—and it was seditious at once.

sentences.zh: 轍諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhe remonstrated saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhe remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 「伏見御試策題，歷詆近歲行事，有紹復熙寧、元豐之意。

translations.literal: " Your subject ventures to see the imperial examination policy topic—it throughout denounces recent years' conduct and has intent to continue and restore Xining and Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: " I see that the imperial examination topic denounces recent policy and hints at restoring Xining and Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 臣謂先帝以天縱之才，行大有為之志，其所設施，度越前古，蓋有百世不可改者。

translations.literal: Your subject says the former emperor by heaven-endowed talent pursued a great active-will; what he established and practiced surpassed former antiquity—probably there are matters a hundred generations cannot change.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor possessed heaven-given talent and pursued great reform; much that he enacted surpassed antiquity and should stand for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 在位近二十年，而終身不受尊號。

translations.literal: On the throne nearly twenty years, yet in his whole life he did not accept an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned nearly twenty years yet never accepted an honorific title in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 裁損宗室，恩止袒免，減朝廷無窮之費。

translations.literal: He cut and reduced the imperial clan; favor stopped at unlined garment exemption, reducing the court's endless expense.
translations.idiomatic: He trimmed the imperial clan so favors stopped at mourning-garment exemption, cutting endless court expense.

sentences.zh: 出賣坊場，顧募衙前，免民間破家之患。

translations.literal: He sold market stalls and hired yamen runners, freeing the people from the affliction of ruined households.
translations.idiomatic: He sold market stalls to hire yamen runners and spared the people ruined households.

sentences.zh: 黜罷諸科誦數之學，訓練諸將慵惰之兵。

translations.literal: He dismissed and abolished the various examination routes of recitation and reckoning study, and trained generals' lazy and idle troops.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished rote examination tracks and trained the generals' slack troops.

sentences.zh: 置寄祿之官，復六曹之舊，嚴重祿之法，禁交謁之私。

translations.literal: He established salary-only offices, restored the six ministries' old forms, strictly weighted salary law, and forbade private exchange visits.
translations.idiomatic: He created salary-only posts, restored the six ministries, tightened salary law, and banned private lobbying.

sentences.zh: 行淺攻之策以制西夏，收六色之錢以寬雜役。

translations.literal: He practiced shallow-attack strategy to control Western Xia and collected six-color money to ease miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He used limited campaigns to restrain Xi Xia and collected the six-color tax to ease miscellaneous labor duties.

sentences.zh: 凡如此類，皆先帝之睿算，有利無害，而元祐以來，上下奉行，未嘗失墜也。

translations.literal: All such kinds were the former emperor's sage reckoning—beneficial without harm—and since Yuanyou above and below have practiced them, never once failing and falling.
translations.idiomatic: Measures like these were the late emperor's wise calculations, beneficial and harmless; since Yuanyou court and country have upheld them without lapse.

sentences.zh: 至於其他，事有失當，何世無之。

translations.literal: As for the rest, affairs that miss fittingness—what age lacks them?
translations.idiomatic: As for other policies that missed the mark, what age has lacked those?

sentences.zh: 父作之于前，子救之於後，前後相濟，此則聖人之孝也。

translations.literal: The father made them before, the son rescues after; before and after aid each other—this is the sage's filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The father enacted reforms; the son corrects what must be corrected—each in turn, and that is the sage's filial duty.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝外事四征，內興宮室，財用匱竭，於是修鹽鐵、榷酤、均輸之政，民不堪命，幾至大亂。

translations.literal: Han Emperor Wu on external affairs campaigned in four directions; within he raised palaces; fiscal resources were exhausted—thereupon he repaired salt-iron, monopoly wine, and equal-transport policies; the people could not bear the command and nearly reached great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han campaigned on four fronts and built palaces within until the treasury was drained; he then imposed salt-iron monopolies, wine franchises, and equal-transport levies until the people could hardly endure it and the realm nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 昭帝委任霍光，罷去煩苛，漢室乃定。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao entrusted Huo Guang, abolished troublesome severity, and the Han house was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhao entrusted Huo Guang, who abolished harsh measures, and the Han house was stabilized.

sentences.zh: 光武、顯宗以察為明，以讖決事，上下恐懼，人懷不安。

translations.literal: Guangwu and Mingzong took scrutiny as clarity and used prognostic texts to decide affairs; above and below were in fear, people harbored unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu and Mingzong prized minute scrutiny and decided affairs by omens; court and country lived in fear and unease.

sentences.zh: 章帝即位，深鑒其失，代之以寬厚、愷悌之政，後世稱焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang acceded, deeply mirrored their errors, and replaced them with generous, mild, and kind government—later ages praise it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhang came to the throne he deeply reflected on those errors and replaced them with generous and humane government, which later ages praised.

sentences.zh: 本朝真宗右文偃武，號稱太平，而群臣因其極盛，為天書之說。

translations.literal: In our dynasty Zhenzong honored culture and rested arms, called Great Peace, yet the various ministers because of its extreme flourishing made the Heavenly Writings doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Our Zhenzong honored culture over arms and was hailed for Great Peace, yet ministers at the height of prosperity preached the Heavenly Writings.

sentences.zh: 章獻臨御，攬大臣之議，藏書梓宮，以泯其跡；

translations.literal: Zhangxian held the throne, gathered great ministers' deliberation, stored the books in the spirit palace to erase their traces;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangxian took power, accepted ministers' counsel, and buried the texts in the spirit palace to erase the episode;

sentences.zh: 及仁宗聽政，絕口不言。

translations.literal: when Renzong heard government, he closed his mouth and did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: when Renzong began to rule, he never spoke of it again.

sentences.zh: 英宗自藩邸入繼，大臣創濮廟之議。

translations.literal: Yingzong from the princely residence entered to succeed; great ministers created the Pu Temple deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong succeeded from the princely establishment, and ministers raised the Pu Temple controversy.

sentences.zh: 及先帝嗣位，或請復舉其事，寢而不答，遂以安靜。

translations.literal: When the former emperor succeeded the throne, some asked to revive the affair; he laid it aside without answer, and thereby there was quiet.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor succeeded, some asked to revive the issue; he ignored it, and the court remained calm.

sentences.zh: 夫以漢昭、章之賢，與吾仁宗、神宗之聖，豈其薄於孝敬而輕事變易也哉？

translations.literal: Considering the worth of Han Zhao and Zhang, and our Renzong and Shenzong's sagehood—how could they be thin in filial respect and light in changing affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Were Han Zhao and Zhang, or our Renzong and Shenzong, deficient in filial piety or careless about change?

sentences.zh: 臣不勝區區，願陛下反覆臣言，慎勿輕事改易。

translations.literal: Your subject cannot bear his slight portion; I wish Your Majesty to turn over your subject's words again and carefully not lightly change affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh my words again and not lightly overturn established policy.

sentences.zh: 若輕變九年已行之事，擢任累歲不用之人，人懷私忿，而以先帝為辭，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If one lightly changes what has been practiced nine years, promotes and employs men unused for accumulated years—people harbor private resentment and take the former emperor as pretext—the great affair is lost."
translations.idiomatic: If you lightly overturn nine years of settled policy and elevate men long out of favor, men will nurse private grudges under the late emperor's name, and the great cause will be lost."

sentences.zh: 轍性沉靜簡潔，為文汪洋澹泊，似其為人，不願人知之，而秀傑之氣終不可掩，其高處殆與兄軾相迫。

translations.literal: Zhe's nature was calm and quiet, simple and concise; his writing vast and mild, light and plain, like his person—unwilling that people know him, yet outstanding and heroic qi in the end could not be covered; his high places nearly pressed his elder brother Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe was calm and spare; his prose was vast yet plain, like the man himself—he did not seek renown, yet his brilliance could not be hidden, and at his best he nearly matched his brother Shi.

sentences.zh: 所著《詩傳》、《春秋傳》、《古史》、《老子解》、《欒城文集》並行於世。

translations.literal: What he authored—the Commentary on the Odes, Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, Ancient History, Explication of Laozi, and Luancheng Collected Works—all circulated in the world together.
translations.idiomatic: His Commentary on the Odes, Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, Ancient History, Explication of Laozi, and Luancheng Collected Works all circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 三子：遲、適、遜。

translations.literal: Three sons: Chi, Shi, and Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Chi, Shi, and Xun.

sentences.zh: 族孫元老。

translations.literal: Clan grandson Yuanlao.
translations.idiomatic: His clan grandson was Yuanlao.

sentences.zh: 族孫 元老

translations.literal: Clan grandson Yuanlao
translations.idiomatic: Clan grandson Yuanlao

sentences.zh: 元老，字子廷。

translations.literal: Yuanlao, style name Ziting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlao, courtesy name Ziting.

sentences.zh: 幼孤力學，長於《春秋》，善屬文。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he studied with force; skilled in the Spring and Autumn, good at composing writing.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he studied hard, excelled in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 軾謫居海上，數以書往來。

translations.literal: Shi, demoted to dwell on the sea, several times exchanged letters.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, exiled to the coast, exchanged letters with him often.

sentences.zh: 軾喜其為學有功，轍亦愛獎之。

translations.literal: Shi was pleased that his study had achievement; Zhe also loved and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was pleased with his scholarly progress, and Zhe also encouraged him warmly.

sentences.zh: 黃庭堅見而奇之，曰：「此蘇氏之秀也。」

translations.literal: Huang Tingjian saw him and marveled, saying: "This is the Su clan's outstanding talent."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tingjian saw him and exclaimed, "Here is the Su family's finest sprout."

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調廣都簿，歷漢州教授、西京國子博士、通判彭州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was assigned Guangdu registrar, and served as Hanzhou professor, Western Capital National University academician, and Tongpan of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as registrar of Guangdu, then as professor at Hanzhou, academician at the Western Capital National University, and assistant prefect of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 政和間，宰相喜開邊西南，帥臣多啖誘近界諸族使納土，分置郡縣以為功，致茂州蠻叛，帥司遽下令招降。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era the chief minister delighted in opening the southwestern border; frontier commanders mostly enticed and induced near-border tribes to submit territory, divided and placed prefectures and counties for merit, causing Maozhou barbarians to rebel; the command bureau hastily ordered surrender recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenghe the chief minister favored expanding the southwest frontier; commanders often enticed border tribes to submit land and carved out counties for credit, until the Maozhou tribes rebelled and the command hurriedly ordered them to surrender.

sentences.zh: 元老歎曰：「威不足以服，則恩不足以懷。」

translations.literal: Yuanlao sighed: "If awe is insufficient to subdue, then grace is insufficient to win hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlao sighed, "If awe cannot subdue them, grace cannot win their hearts."

sentences.zh: 乃移書成都帥周燾曰：「此蠻跳樑山谷間，伺間竊發。

translations.literal: He then sent a letter to Chengdu commander Zhou Tao saying: "These barbarians leap beams in mountain valleys, watch for openings and steal to rise.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Zhou Tao, commander of Chengdu: "These tribes roam the mountains and strike when they see an opening.

sentences.zh: 彼之所長，我之所短，惟施、黔兩州兵可與為敵。

translations.literal: What they excel at is what we lack; only Shi and Qian two prefectures' troops can be their match.
translations.idiomatic: Their strengths are our weaknesses; only troops from Shi and Qian prefectures can match them.

sentences.zh: 若檄數千人，使倍道往赴，賢於官軍十萬也。

translations.literal: If one issues orders to several thousand men and makes them go by double marches, it is better than a hundred thousand government troops.
translations.idiomatic: If we dispatch a few thousand men by forced marches, that would be worth more than a hundred thousand regular troops.

sentences.zh: 其次以為夔、陝兵大集，先以夔兵誘其前，陝兵從其後，不十日，賊必破。

translations.literal: Next I consider that Kui and Shan troops mass greatly—first use Kui troops to lure their front, Shan troops follow their rear; within ten days the bandits will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Next, mass Kui and Shan troops: lure them with Kui forces in front and strike from behind with Shan troops—in ten days the rebels will break.

sentences.zh: 彼降而我受焉，則威懷之道得。

translations.literal: When they surrender and we receive them, then the way of awe and winning hearts is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When they surrender and we accept them, awe and grace will both be served.

sentences.zh: 今不討賊，既招而還，必復叛，不免重用兵矣。」

translations.literal: Now not punishing the bandits, yet recruiting surrender and returning—they will surely rebel again and cannot avoid again using troops heavily."
translations.idiomatic: If we do not punish them now but recruit surrender and withdraw, they will rebel again and we will have to fight anew."

sentences.zh: 燾得書，即召與計事。

translations.literal: Tao received the letter and at once summoned him to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tao received the letter and summoned him to counsel at once.

sentences.zh: 元老又策：「茂有兩道，正道自濕山趨長平，絕嶺而上，其路險以高；

translations.literal: Yuanlao again strategized: "Mao has two routes—the main route from Wet Mountain toward Changping, crossing ridges to ascend; its road is dangerous and high;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlao added, "Mao has two routes: the main road from Wet Mountain toward Changping climbs dangerous ridges;

sentences.zh: 間道自青崖關趨刁溪，循江而行，其路夷以徑。

translations.literal: the side route from Qingya Pass toward Diaoxi, following the river to go—its road is level and direct.
translations.idiomatic: the side road from Qingya Pass to Diaoxi follows the river and is level and direct.

sentences.zh: 當使正兵陣濕山，而陰出奇兵搗刁溪，與石泉並力合攻，賊腹背受敵，擒之必矣。」

translations.literal: One should make the main force array at Wet Mountain while secretly sending extraordinary troops to strike Diaoxi; together with Shiquan combine strength to attack together—the bandits will be attacked belly and back and capture is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Post the main force at Wet Mountain while secretly striking Diaoxi; join Shiquan in a combined attack and the rebels will be caught front and rear—capture is certain."

sentences.zh: 燾皆不能用，竟得罪。

translations.literal: Tao could use none of it and in the end suffered offense.
translations.idiomatic: Tao used none of it, and Yuanlao was punished in the end.

sentences.zh: 後帥至，如元老策，蠻勢蹙，乃降。

translations.literal: Later when a commander arrived and followed Yuanlao's strategy, the barbarian momentum was pressed and they then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the next commander arrived and followed Yuanlao's plan, the tribes were cornered and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 除國子博士，歷秘書正字、將作少監、比部考功員外郎，尋除成都路轉運副使，為軍器監，司農、衛尉、太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed National University academician, served as Secretariat corrector, Assistant Director of Imperial Works, Revenue Ministry and Merit Evaluation outer section member; shortly after was appointed Chengdu Circuit transport vice commissioner, became Armaments Director, and Agriculture, Guards, and Rites Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was made National University academician, then Secretariat corrector, Assistant Director of Imperial Works, and outer-section member in the Revenue and Merit Evaluation bureaus; later transport vice commissioner on the Chengdu circuit, Armaments Director, and vice ministers of Agriculture, Guards, and Rites.

sentences.zh: 元老外和內勁，不妄與人交。

translations.literal: Yuanlao outwardly was mild and inwardly was firm; he did not rashly associate with people.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlao was outwardly mild and inwardly firm and did not make friends lightly.

sentences.zh: 梁師成方用事，自言為軾外子，因緣欲見之，且求其文，拒不答。

translations.literal: Liang Shicheng was then in power, saying himself he was Shi's son by a concubine; by connection he wished to see him and also asked for his writings—he refused and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shicheng was then in power and claimed to be Shi's son by a concubine; he sought a meeting and asked for writings, but Yuanlao refused.

sentences.zh: 言者遂論元老蘇軾從孫，且為元祐邪說，其學術議論，頗仿軾、轍，不宜在中朝。

translations.literal: Memorializers thereupon argued Yuanlao was Su Shi's collateral grandson and moreover held Yuanyou perverse talk; his learning and deliberation largely imitated Shi and Zhe—he was not fitting in the central court.
translations.idiomatic: Critics then argued that Yuanlao, as Su Shi's collateral grandson, held Yuanyou heterodoxy and imitated Shi and Zhe in learning and opinion, and should not serve at court.

sentences.zh: 罷為提點明道宮。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to be Intendant of the Mingdao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to serve as intendant of the Mingdao Palace.

sentences.zh: 元老歎曰：「昔顏子附驥尾而名顯，吾今以家世坐累，榮矣。」

translations.literal: Yuanlao sighed: "Formerly Yanzi attached to a thoroughbred's tail and his name was displayed; I today sit in trouble because of family and generation—honored indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlao sighed, "Yan Hui once rode a thoroughbred's tail to fame; I am now honored to suffer for my family name."

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: Before long he died, age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 有詩文行于時。

translations.literal: He had poetry and prose circulating in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 論曰：蘇轍論事精確，修辭簡嚴，未必劣于其兄。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Su Zhe in deliberating affairs was precise; in polishing writing, simple and strict—not necessarily inferior to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The historians judge that Su Zhe's policy analysis was precise and his prose spare and rigorous—not necessarily beneath his brother's.

sentences.zh: 王安石初議青苗，轍數語柅之，安石自是不復及此，後非王廣廉傅會，則此議息矣。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi first deliberated Green Sprouts, Zhe with a few words checked it; Anshi from this did not again touch it—later if not for Wang Guanglian's forced alignment, then this deliberation would have ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi first proposed Green Sprouts, Zhe checked him in a few words and Anshi dropped the subject; had Wang Guanglian not forced the issue later, the scheme would have died.

sentences.zh: 轍寡言鮮欲，素有以得安石之敬心，故能爾也。

translations.literal: Zhe spoke little and had few desires; he always had means to obtain Anshi's respectful heart—therefore he could be so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe spoke little and wanted little, and had long earned Anshi's respect—hence he could speak so frankly.

sentences.zh: 若是者，軾宜若不及，然至論軾英邁之氣，閎肆之文，轍為軾弟，可謂難矣。

translations.literal: In such matters Shi ought to seem as if he could not reach it; yet when it comes to discussing Shi's heroic surpassing qi and grand, expansive writing—as Zhe was Shi's younger brother, one may say it was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: In such matters Shi might seem unmatched; yet in heroic breadth and expansive prose, for Zhe as his younger brother to stand near him was no small feat.

sentences.zh: 元祐秉政，力斥章、蔡，不主調停；

translations.literal: In Yuanyou holding government he forcefully expelled Zhang and Cai and did not uphold mediation;
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanyou he forcefully opposed Zhang and Cai and rejected mediation;

sentences.zh: 及議回河、雇役，與文彥博、司馬光異同；

translations.literal: when deliberating returning the river and hired service, he differed and agreed with Wen Yanbo and Sima Guang;
translations.idiomatic: on the Yellow River return and hired service he differed from Wen Yanbo and Sima Guang;

sentences.zh: 西邊之謀，又與呂大防、劉摯不合。

translations.literal: on western border schemes he again did not agree with Lü Dafang and Liu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: and on western frontier policy he again disagreed with Lü Dafang and Liu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 君子不黨，於轍見之。

translations.literal: The gentleman does not form factions—in Zhe this is seen.
translations.idiomatic: That a gentleman does not cling to faction is seen in Zhe.

sentences.zh: 轍與兄進退出處，無不相同，患難之中，友愛彌篤，無少怨尤，近古罕見。

translations.literal: Zhe and his elder brother in advance, retreat, going out and dwelling were without not the same; in hardship their friendship and love grew more earnest, without slight resentment—rare in recent antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe and his brother advanced and retreated alike; in hardship their affection only deepened without a trace of resentment—rare in recent ages.

sentences.zh: 獨其齒爵皆優於兄，意者造物之所賦與，亦有乘除於其間哉！

translations.literal: Only his age and rank were all superior to his elder brother—perhaps creation's gift, yet also there is multiplication and division between them!
translations.idiomatic: Only his years and offices outranked his brother's—perhaps heaven's allotment, yet fortune has its reckonings between them as well!
